nodes.name: Proof of Lemma F.6
nodes.statement:
We compute the time derivative of the loss along the gradient flow in three substantive steps: (i) chain rule across all layers; (ii) substitution of $\dot W_{(
u)} = -
abla_W {\cal L}$ and $\dot U_{(
u)} = -
abla_U {\cal L}$; (iii) regrouping the resulting quadratic form using the layer-wise kernel matrices $H_{(
u)}(t)$. We have:  egin{align*} {\mathbb{E}}\Big[ rac{\mathrm{d} }{\mathrm{d} t}{\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})\Big] = & ~ {\mathbb{E}}\Big[\sum_{
u=1}^N \Big(\Big\langle rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{vec}(W_{(
u)}(t))},  rac{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{vec}(W_{(
u)}(t))}{\mathrm{d} t}\Bigangle + \Big\langle rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{vec}(U_{(
u)}(t))},  rac{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{vec}(U_{(
u)}(t))}{\mathrm{d} t}\Bigangle\Big)\Big] \ = & ~ -\sum_{
u=1}^N \Big(\Big\| rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{vec}(W_{(
u)}(t))}\Big\|_2^2 + \Big\| rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{vec}(U_{(
u)}(t))}\Big\|_2^2\Big) \ = & ~- \sum_{
u=1}^N \sum_{p=1}^{nL} \sum_{q=1}^{nL} \Big\langle  rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mu_{(
u), p}(t)},  ig(\langle  eta_{(
u), p}(t),  eta_{(
u), q}(t) angle + \langle \gamma_{(
u), p}(t), \gamma_{(
u), q}(t) angle  ig) \cdot I_d  rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mu_{(
u), q}(t)} \Bigangle \ = & ~ - \sum_{
u \in [N]} \mathrm{vec}\Big( rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mu_{(
u)}(t)}\Big)^	op \cdot  ig( H_{(
u)}(t) \otimes I_d  ig) \cdot \mathrm{vec}\Big( rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mu_{(
u)}(t)}\Big), \end{align*} where the first step follows from the multivariable chain rule applied across the parameter sets $\{W_{(
u)}, U_{(
u)}\}_{
u\in[N]}$, the second step follows from the gradient-flow update Equation~\eqref{eq:ODE_update}, which sets $\dot W_{(
u)} = -
abla_W {\cal L}$ and $\dot U_{(
u)} = -
abla_U {\cal L}$, so $\langle
abla_W {\cal L}, \dot W_{(
u)}angle = -\|
abla_W {\cal L}\|_2^2$ (likewise for $U$). The third step follows from Parts 1, 2, and 3 of Lemma~ef{lem:grad_computation}, which express each parameter-space gradient as a sum-over-tokens product involving the kernel features $ eta_{(
u),p}(t)$ and $\gamma_{(
u),p}(t)$, paired with $ rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}}{\mathrm{d} \mu_{(
u),p}(t)}$. The last step follows from the definition $H_{(
u),p,q}(t) = \langle eta_{(
u),p}, eta_{(
u),q}angle + \langle\gamma_{(
u),p},\gamma_{(
u),q}angle$ and the standard tensor identity $\sum_{p,q} a_p^	op H_{p,q}\, I_d\, a_q = \mathrm{vec}(a)^	op (H\otimes I_d) \mathrm{vec}(a)$, where the row-major $\mathrm{vec}$ convention of Section~ef{sub:notations} is used so that $\mathrm{vec}(a)$ stacks the rows $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{nL}\in\mathbb{R}^d$ end-to-end into an $nLd$-vector. The Kronecker structure $H\otimes I_d$ matches this convention because the row-by-row layout commutes with the per-row $I_d$.
nodes.statement_short: Chain rule across layers, substitute the gradient-flow update, and regroup into kernel quadratic forms.

nodes.name: Plan
nodes.statement:
We compute the time derivative of the loss along the gradient flow in three substantive steps: (i) chain rule across all layers; (ii) substitution of $\dot W_{(
u)} = -
abla_W {\cal L}$ and $\dot U_{(
u)} = -
abla_U {\cal L}$; (iii) regrouping the resulting quadratic form using the layer-wise kernel matrices $H_{(
u)}(t)$.
nodes.statement_short: Three steps: chain rule, substitute gradient flow, regroup

nodes.name: Chain rule and gradient flow
nodes.statement:
We have:
     egin{align*}
        {\mathbb{E}}\Big[ rac{\mathrm{d} }{\mathrm{d} t}{\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})\Big]
        = & ~ {\mathbb{E}}\Big[\sum_{
u=1}^N \Big(\Big\langle rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{vec}(W_{(
u)}(t))},  rac{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{vec}(W_{(
u)}(t))}{\mathrm{d} t}\Bigangle + \Big\langle rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{vec}(U_{(
u)}(t))},  rac{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{vec}(U_{(
u)}(t))}{\mathrm{d} t}\Bigangle\Big)\Big] \
        = & ~ -\sum_{
u=1}^N \Big(\Big\| rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{vec}(W_{(
u)}(t))}\Big\|_2^2 + \Big\| rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mathrm{vec}(U_{(
u)}(t))}\Big\|_2^2\Big) \
        = &  ~- \sum_{
u=1}^N \sum_{p=1}^{nL} \sum_{q=1}^{nL} \Big\langle  rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mu_{(
u), p}(t)},  ig(\langle  eta_{(
u), p}(t),  eta_{(
u), q}(t) angle + \langle \gamma_{(
u), p}(t), \gamma_{(
u), q}(t) angle  ig) \cdot I_d  rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mu_{(
u), q}(t)} \Bigangle \
        = & ~ - \sum_{
u \in [N]} \mathrm{vec}\Big( rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mu_{(
u)}(t)}\Big)^	op \cdot  ig( H_{(
u)}(t) \otimes I_d  ig) \cdot  \mathrm{vec}\Big( rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mu_{(
u)}(t)}\Big),
    \end{align*}
    where the first step follows from the multivariable chain rule applied across the parameter sets $\{W_{(
u)}, U_{(
u)}\}_{
u\in[N]}$, the second step follows from the gradient-flow update Equation~\eqref{eq:ODE_update}, which sets $\dot W_{(
u)} = -
abla_W {\cal L}$ and $\dot U_{(
u)} = -
abla_U {\cal L}$, so $\langle
abla_W {\cal L}, \dot W_{(
u)}angle = -\|
abla_W {\cal L}\|_2^2$ (likewise for $U$).
nodes.statement_short: Expand $\dot{\cal L}$ and substitute the gradient-flow update

nodes.name: Kernel features
nodes.statement:
The third step follows from Parts 1, 2, and 3 of Lemma~ef{lem:grad_computation}, which express each parameter-space gradient as a sum-over-tokens product involving the kernel features $ eta_{(
u),p}(t)$ and $\gamma_{(
u),p}(t)$, paired with $ rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}}{\mathrm{d} \mu_{(
u),p}(t)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Gradients factor through the kernel features (Lemma F.4)

nodes.name: Regroup
nodes.statement:
The last step follows from the definition $H_{(
u),p,q}(t) = \langle eta_{(
u),p}, eta_{(
u),q}angle + \langle\gamma_{(
u),p},\gamma_{(
u),q}angle$ and the standard tensor identity $\sum_{p,q} a_p^	op H_{p,q}\, I_d\, a_q = \mathrm{vec}(a)^	op (H\otimes I_d) \mathrm{vec}(a)$, where the row-major $\mathrm{vec}$ convention of Section~ef{sub:notations} is used so that $\mathrm{vec}(a)$ stacks the rows $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_{nL}\in\mathbb{R}^d$ end-to-end into an $nLd$-vector. The Kronecker structure $H\otimes I_d$ matches this convention because the row-by-row layout commutes with the per-row $I_d$.
nodes.statement_short: Regroup with $H_{(\nu)}$ and the Kronecker identity

nodes.name: Helpful bounds
nodes.statement:
Denote failure probability $\delta \in (0, 0.1)$. Define $B := \max\{O(\sqrt{\log(Nmd/\delta)}), 1\}$. Assuming there exists a constant $R \in (0, 1)$ satisfying $\| w_{(
u), r}(t) - w_{(
u), r}(0) \|_2 \leq R$ and $\| U_{(
u)}(t) - U_{(
u)}(0)\|_F \leq R$ for $r \in [m]$ and $
u \in [N]$ and $R \in (0, 1)$. We mark the indices as: $r\in [m]$, $p \in [nL]$, $\ell_1, \ell_2 \in [L]$, and $
u \in [N]$. We denote $i = \lfloor p / L floor$, $\ell = p {m ~ mod~} L$, $\ell' \in [\ell]$. If Definition~ef{def:gd} holds, then with a probability at least $1 - \delta$, we have:  egin{itemize} \item {m Basic Bounds.}  egin{itemize} \item { f Part 1.} $\| w_{(
u), r}(0) \|_2 \leq O(\sqrt{d}B)$. \item { f Part 2.} $\| U_{(
u)}(0) \|_F \leq O(dB)$. \item { f Part 3.} $\| w_{(
u), r}(t) \|_2 \leq O(\sqrt{d}B)$. \item { f Part 4.} $\| U_{(
u)}(t) \|_F \leq O(dB)$. \item { f Part 5.} $\| \Lambda_{(
u), i, \ell}(t) \|_2 = \Theta(1)$ for all $\ell \in [L]$. \item { f Part 6.} $\| \Lambda_{(
u), i}(t) U_{(
u)}(t) \Lambda_{(
u), i}(t)^	op \|_\infty \leq O(dB)$. \item { f Part 7.} $ \exp ig( [\Lambda_{(
u), i}(t) U_{(
u)}(t) \Lambda_{(
u), i}(t)^	op]_{\ell_1, \ell_2}  ig) \in [ \exp(-O(dB)), \exp(O(dB)) ]$ for all $\ell_1, \ell_2 \in [L]$. \item { f Part 8.} For $\ell'\in [\ell]$, $ \sigma_{(
u), p, \ell'}(t) \in [\exp(-O(dB)) / L, 1]$. \end{itemize} \item {m Perturbation Bounds.}  egin{itemize} \item { f Part 9.} $\| w_{(
u), r}(t) - w_{(
u), r}(0) \|_2 \leq R$. \item { f Part 10.} $\| U_{(
u)}(t) - U_{(
u)}(0)\|_F \leq R$. \item { f Part 11.} $\| \Lambda_{(
u), i, \ell}(t) - \Lambda_{(
u), i, \ell}(0)\|_2 \leq O(R)$. \item { f Part 12.} $\| \sigma_{(
u), p}(t) - \sigma_{(
u), p}(0) \|_2 \leq O(\sqrt{L}R)$. \item { f Part 13.} $\| o_{(
u), p}(t) - o_{(
u), p}(0) \|_2 \leq O(\sqrt{L}R)$. \end{itemize} \item {m Gradient and Function Norms.}  egin{itemize} \item { f Part 14.} ${\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D}) \leq O(Ld)$. \item { f Part 15.} $\|  rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mu_{(
u)}(t)} \|_F^2 \asymp  rac{\varepsilon^2}{n} \cdot {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})$. {\it (Note: the $1/n$ factor is essential and traces directly to the $ rac{1}{n}$ in the loss definition $\mathcal{L} =  rac{1}{n}\|\mathsf{F}-\mathsf{Y}\|_F^2$. See proof below.)} \item { f Part 16.} $\| \gamma_{(
u), p}(t) \|_2 \leq o(1/\sqrt{m})$. \end{itemize} \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Sixteen high-probability bounds on weights, hidden states, attention scores, their drifts, the loss and the hidden-state gradients inside the lazy ball.
assumptions:
Assuming there exists a constant $R \in (0, 1)$ satisfying $\| w_{(
u), r}(t) - w_{(
u), r}(0) \|_2 \leq R$ and $\| U_{(
u)}(t) - U_{(
u)}(0)\|_F \leq R$
If Definition~\ref{def:gd} holds
nodes.label: lem:helpful_bounds

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma G.1
nodes.statement:
{ f Proof of Part 1.} Each entry $w_{(
u),r,k}(0)$ is i.i.d.\ $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ by initialization. By Fact~ef{fac:gaussian_tail}, $|w_{(
u),r,k}(0)| \le C\sqrt{\log(Nmd/\delta)}$ with probability at least $1 - \delta/(Nmd)$. A union bound over $
u\in[N], r\in[m], k\in[d]$ shows that all entries are bounded by $C\sqrt{\log(Nmd/\delta)}$ simultaneously with probability at least $1-\delta$. Thus $\|w_{(
u),r}(0)\|_2^2 = \sum_{k\in[d]} w_{(
u),r,k}(0)^2 \le d \cdot C^2\log(Nmd/\delta) = O(d B^2)$, giving $\|w_{(
u),r}(0)\|_2 \le O(\sqrt d B)$. { f Proof of Part 2.} Analogously, each entry $U_{(
u),k_1,k_2}(0)$ is i.i.d.\ $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$. By Fact~ef{fac:gaussian_tail} and a union bound over $
u\in[N], (k_1,k_2)\in[d]	imes[d]$, all entries are bounded by $O(B)$ with probability at least $1-\delta$. Therefore $\|U_{(
u)}(0)\|_F^2 = \sum_{k_1,k_2} U_{(
u),k_1,k_2}(0)^2 \le d^2\cdot O(B^2) = O(d^2 B^2)$, hence $\|U_{(
u)}(0)\|_F \le O(dB)$. { f Proof of Part 3.} By triangle inequality, $\|w_{(
u),r}(t)\|_2 \le \|w_{(
u),r}(0)\|_2 + \|w_{(
u),r}(t)-w_{(
u),r}(0)\|_2 \le O(\sqrt dB) + R$ from Part~1 and the lemma's hypothesis. Since $R \in (0,1)$ and $B\ge 1$ (so $\sqrt d B\ge 1$), the second summand is dominated and $\|w_{(
u),r}(t)\|_2 \le O(\sqrt d B)$. { f Proof of Part 4.} Analogously to Part~3, $\|U_{(
u)}(t)\|_F \le \|U_{(
u)}(0)\|_F + \|U_{(
u)}(t)-U_{(
u)}(0)\|_F \le O(dB) + R$, and the second summand is dominated by the first under $R\in(0,1)$ and $B\ge 1$, giving $\|U_{(
u)}(t)\|_F \le O(dB)$. { f Proof of Part 5.} Because $A_{(
u)}$ is trained jointly with $W_{(
u)},U_{(
u)}$ by gradient flow (Section~ef{sec:preli}), the entries $a_{(
u),r,k}(t)$ are no longer in $\{-1,+1\}$ for $t>0$ and are in general not independent of $w_{(
u),r}(t)$. We therefore prove Part~5 in two steps: first at the initialization time $t=0$ via Hoeffding (where the i.i.d.\ $\pm 1$ assumption holds), then for $t>0$ via the perturbation bound of Part~13 of this lemma and the FFN-drift bound of Lemma~ef{lem:ffn_drift}. {\it Step 1: $
u=1$ at $t=0$.} The data assumption (Section~ef{sub:setups}) gives $\|\Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}\|_2 = \|X_{i,\ell}+E_\ell\|_2 = \Theta(1)$ for every $\ell$. Combined with the fact that $\sigma_{(1), p}(0)$ is a probability vector,  egin{align*} \|o_{(1), p}(0)\|_2 = \|\Lambda_{(0), i}(0)^	op \sigma_{(1), p}(0)\|_2 \le \max_{\ell'} \|\Lambda_{(0), i, \ell'}\|_2 = \Theta(1). \end{align*} For the $\mu$-term at $t=0$, we note that $a_{(1),r,k}(0) \in \{-1,+1\}$ is i.i.d.\ uniform and independent of $w_{(1),r}(0)\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_d)$ (the i.i.d.\ initialization ensures this). Hence, fixing $k\in[d]$ and conditioning on $w_{(1),r}(0)$:  egin{align*} |a_{(1), r, k}(0)\cdot\phi(\langle o_{(1), p}(0), w_{(1), r}(0)angle)| & ~ \le 1\cdot\|w_{(1),r}(0)\|_2\cdot\|o_{(1),p}(0)\|_2 \le O(\sqrt{d}B), \ {\mathbb{E}} ig[a_{(1), r, k}(0)\cdot\phi(\langle o_{(1), p}(0), w_{(1), r}(0)angle)\, ig|\, w_{(1),r}(0) ig] & ~ = {\mathbb{E}}[a_{(1),r,k}(0)]\cdot \phi(\cdot) = 0. \end{align*} By Hoeffding (Lemma~ef{lem:hoeffding}) applied to $\sum_{r=1}^m a_{(1),r,k}(0)\phi(\langle o_{(1),p}(0),w_{(1),r}(0)angle)$, with probability at least $1-\delta/(md)$:  egin{align*} \Big|\sum_{r=1}^m a_{(1), r, k}(0)\phi(\langle o_{(1), p}(0), w_{(1), r}(0)angle)\Big| \le O(\sqrt{md}B)\sqrt{\log(md/\delta)} \le O(\sqrt{m}\,\sqrt{d}\,B^2). \end{align*} Taking the union bound over $k\in[d]$:  egin{align*} \|\mu_{(1), p}(0)\|_2 \le  rac{\omega\sqrt d}{\sqrt m}\max_{k\in[d]}\Big|\sum_r a_{(1),r,k}(0)\phi(\cdot)\Big| \le O(\omega\, d\, B^2), \end{align*} and therefore  egin{align*} \|\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0)\|_2 \le \|\Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(0)\|_2 + \|\mu_{(1), p}(0)\|_2 \le \Theta(1) + O(\omega d B^2) = \Theta(1)\pm o(1/N), \end{align*} where the last step uses $\omega = o(1/(NdB^2))$ from Definition~ef{def:gd}. {\it Step 2: Extension from $t=0$ to $t>0$.} By Parts~9, 10 and~13 of this lemma (proven below), $\|w_{(1),r}(t)-w_{(1),r}(0)\|_2 \le R$ and $\|o_{(1),p}(t)-o_{(1),p}(0)\|_2 \le O(\sqrt L R)$. By Lemma~ef{lem:ffn_drift}, $\|A_{(
u)}(t) - A_{(
u)}(0)\|_F \le R_A := O(1/(\sqrt m\,\omega\lambda N))$. The Lipschitz expansion of the layer-1 hidden state with respect to $(W,A,o)$ then gives:  egin{align*} \|\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t) - \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0)\|_2 &\le  rac{\omega}{\sqrt m}\,\Big( \|A_{(1)}(t) - A_{(1)}(0)\|_F\cdot \max_r |\phi(\langle w_{(1),r}(t),o_{(1),p}(t)angle)| \ &\quad+ \|A_{(1)}(0)\|_F\cdot  ig[\max_r \|w_{(1),r}(t)-w_{(1),r}(0)\|_2\cdot \|o_{(1),p}(t)\|_2 + \cdots ig]\Big) \ &\le  rac{\omega}{\sqrt m} ig( R_A\cdot O(\sqrt d B) + O(\sqrt{md})\cdot O(R)  ig) \ &= O\Big( rac{\omega\sqrt d B}{\sqrt m\,\omega\lambda N}\Big) + O(\omega\sqrt d\, R) = o(1) \end{align*} under the strengthened width condition of Lemma~ef{lem:ffn_drift}. Combining with Step~1:  egin{align*} \|\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t)\|_2 \le \|\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0)\|_2 + o(1) = \Theta(1). \end{align*} {\it Step 3: Inductive step ($
u \ge 2$).} Assume the bound holds for layer $
u-1$. Then $\|\Lambda_{(
u-1),i,\ell}(t)\|_2 = \Theta(1)$ uniformly in $\ell$ and $t$, hence $\|o_{(
u),p}(t)\|_2 = \|\Lambda_{(
u-1),i}(t)^	op\sigma_{(
u),p}(t)\|_2 \le \max_{\ell'}\|\Lambda_{(
u-1),i,\ell'}(t)\|_2 = \Theta(1)$. The Hoeffding-then-perturb argument of Steps~1 and~2 applies verbatim to $\mu_{(
u),p}$ (with all quantities re-indexed to layer $
u$), giving $\|\Lambda_{(
u),i,\ell}(t)\|_2 = \Theta(1)$ as claimed. The bound on $\|o_{(
u),p}(t)\|_2$ follows directly:  egin{align} \|o_{(
u), p}(t)\|_2 = \Theta(1). \end{align} { f Proof of Part 6.} We have:  egin{align*} \| \Lambda_{(
u), i}(t) U_{(
u)}(t) \Lambda_{(
u), i}(t)^	op \|_\infty = & ~ \max_{(\ell_1, \ell_2) \in [L] 	imes [L]} \left| \Lambda_{(
u), i, \ell_1}(t)^	op U_{(
u)}(t) \Lambda_{(
u), i, \ell_2}(t) ight| \ \leq & ~ O(dB) \end{align*} where the first step follows from simple algebra, the second step follows from Part 4 and Part 5 of this lemma and Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. { f Proof of Part 7.} From Part~6, $\|\Lambda_{(
u),i}(t) U_{(
u)}(t) \Lambda_{(
u),i}(t)^	op\|_\infty \le O(dB)$, so each attention logit $z_{p,\ell'} :=  ig[\Lambda_{(
u),i}(t) U_{(
u)}(t) \Lambda_{(
u),i}(t)^	op ig]_{\ell, \ell'}$ satisfies $|z_{p,\ell'}| \le O(dB)$. Therefore $\exp(z_{p,\ell'}) \in [\exp(-O(dB)), \exp(O(dB))]$, which is the claim. { f Proof of Part 8.} Following Part 7 of this lemma, we can show that:  egin{align*} \sum_{\ell'\in [\ell]} \exp(\Lambda_{(
u), i, \ell}(t)^	op U_{(
u)}(t) \Lambda_{(
u), i, \ell'}(t)) \le \ell \exp(O(dB)) \le L \exp(O(dB)). \end{align*} Then we can show that:  egin{align*} \sigma_{(
u), p, \ell'}(t) \ge & ~ \exp(\Lambda_{(
u), i, \ell}(t)^	op U_{(
u)}(t) \Lambda_{(
u), i, \ell'}(t)) / \sum_{\ell'\in [\ell]} \exp(\Lambda_{(
u), i, \ell}(t)^	op U_{(
u)}(t) \Lambda_{(
u), i, \ell'}(t)) \ \ge & ~  rac{\exp(-O(dB))}{L \exp(O(dB))} \ \ge & ~  rac{\exp(-O(dB))}{L}. \end{align*} Combining the previous results, we obtain the result of this part. { f Proof of Part 9.} This is a direct restatement of the lemma's hypothesis $\|w_{(
u),r}(t) - w_{(
u),r}(0)\|_2 \le R$, which is a bootstrapping assumption that is verified self-consistently in Lemma~ef{lem:perturbations} (where we prove that the gradient flow keeps the iterates inside this ball). { f Proof of Part 10.} Likewise, this is a direct restatement of the hypothesis $\|U_{(
u)}(t) - U_{(
u)}(0)\|_F \le R$, verified self-consistently in Lemma~ef{lem:perturbations}. { f Proof of Part 11, 12 and 13.} We proceed by induction on the layer index $
u$. The base case $
u=0$ is trivial since $\Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(t) = X_{i,\ell} + E_\ell$ does not depend on $t$, and so $\Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(t) = \Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(0)$. {\it Base case: $
u=1$.} By the definition of $\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t)$ as the $\ell$-th token of layer-1 output:  egin{align*} & ~ \| \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t) -\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0)\|_2 \ = & ~ \sqrt{\sum_{k\in [d]} \left( rac{\omega}{\sqrt{m}} \cdot \sum_{r=1}^m a_{(1), r, k} \left(\phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(t), o_{(1), p}(t) angle) - \phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(0), o_{(1), p}(0) angle) ight) ight)^2 }, \end{align*} where the residual connection contributes $\Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(t) - \Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(0) = 0$ and the difference reduces to the FFN-after-attention contribution. We first bound $\|\sigma_{(1),p}(t)-\sigma_{(1),p}(0)\|_2$ via softmax Lipschitzness. Note that $\sigma_{(1),p}(t)$ is a function of the attention logits $\Lambda_{(0), i}(0) U_{(1)}(t)^	op \Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(0) \in \mathbb{R}^L$ (here $\Lambda_{(0), i}(t)=\Lambda_{(0), i}(0)$ is fixed). Hence:  egin{align*} \| \sigma_{(1), p}(t) - \sigma_{(1), p}(0) \|_2 \leq & ~ O(1) \cdot \| \Lambda_{(0), i}(0) ( U_{(1)}(t) - U_{(1)}(0) )^	op \Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(0) \|_2 \ \leq & ~ O(1) \cdot \|\Lambda_{(0), i}(0)\|_F \cdot \| U_{(1)}(t) - U_{(1)}(0) \|_F \cdot \| \Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(0) \|_2 \ \leq & ~ O(1) \cdot O(\sqrt{L}) \cdot R \cdot O(1) = O(\sqrt{L}R), \end{align*} where the first step follows from the definition of $\sigma_{(1), p}(t)$ and Fact~ef{fac:lipschitz_softmax}, the second step from operator-norm submultiplicativity (Cauchy--Schwarz on a quadratic form), the third step from $\|\Lambda_{(0), i}(0)\|_F = O(\sqrt{L})$ (since each token has unit norm, summed over $L$ tokens), $\|U_{(1)}(t) - U_{(1)}(0)\|_F \le R$ (Part 10), and $\|\Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(0)\|_2 = O(1)$. Next, we use the identity $o_{(1),p}(t) = \Lambda_{(0), i}(0)^	op \sigma_{(1), p}(t)$ together with the operator-norm bound $\|\Lambda_{(0),i}(0)\|_{m op} = O(1)$ that follows from the per-token unit-norm constraint $\|X_\ell\|_2 = \Theta(1)$ (Section~ef{sub:setups}) under the residual-and-RMSNorm structure:  egin{align*} \| o_{(1), p}(t) - o_{(1), p}(0) \|_2 = & ~ \| \Lambda_{(0), i}(0)^	op  ig( \sigma_{(1), p}(t) - \sigma_{(1), p}(0)  ig) \|_2 \ \leq & ~ \|\Lambda_{(0), i}(0)\|_{m op} \cdot \| \sigma_{(1), p}(t) - \sigma_{(1), p}(0) \|_2 \ \leq & ~ O(1) \cdot O(\sqrt{L}R) = O(\sqrt{L} R), \end{align*} which matches Part~13. For a fixed index $k \in [d]$, we apply Hoeffding's inequality (Lemma~ef{lem:hoeffding}) to the random variables $a_{(1), r, k} \cdot  ig(\phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(t), o_{(1), p}(t) angle) - \phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(0), o_{(1), p}(0) angle) ig)$ for $r \in [m]$. By Fact~ef{fac:lipschitz_1} (the ReLU $\phi$ is $1$-Lipschitz):  egin{align*} & ~  ig| a_{(1), r, k} \cdot  ig(\phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(t), o_{(1), p}(t) angle) - \phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(0), o_{(1), p}(0) angle) ig)  ig| \ \leq & ~ |a_{(1), r, k}| \cdot  ig| \langle w_{(1), r}(t), o_{(1), p}(t) angle - \langle w_{(1), r}(0), o_{(1), p}(0) angle  ig| \ \leq & ~ 1 \cdot  ig( \| w_{(1), r}(t) - w_{(1), r}(0) \|_2 \cdot \| o_{(1), p}(t) \|_2 + \| w_{(1), r}(0) \|_2 \cdot \| o_{(1), p}(t) - o_{(1), p}(0) \|_2  ig) \ \leq & ~ R \cdot O(1) + O(\sqrt{d} B) \cdot O(\sqrt{L} R) \ \leq & ~ O(\sqrt{Ld}BR), \end{align*} where the second step follows from $|a_{(1),r,k}|=1$ and the bilinear difference identity, the third step from the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality together with the perturbation bounds Part 9 and Part 13 of this lemma, the fourth step from $\|w_{(1),r}(0)\|_2\leq O(\sqrt{d}B)$ (Part 1) and $\|o_{(1),p}(t)\|_2 = O(1)$. The mean is zero since $a_{(1), r, k} \in \{-1,+1\}$ uniformly and is independent of $w$:  egin{align*} {\mathbb{E}} ig[a_{(1), r, k} \cdot  ig( \phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(t), o_{(1), p}(t) angle) - \phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(0), o_{(1), p}(0) angle) ig) ig] = 0. \end{align*} By Lemma~ef{lem:hoeffding}, for any fixed $k$, with probability at least $1 - \delta/(md)$:  egin{align*} & ~ \Big|  rac{\omega}{\sqrt{m}} \sum_{r=1}^m a_{(1), r, k} \cdot  ig(\phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(t), o_{(1), p}(t) angle) - \phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(0), o_{(1), p}(0) angle) ig) \Big| \ & \leq  rac{\omega}{\sqrt{m}}\cdot O(\sqrt{Ld}BR)\cdot\sqrt{m\log(md/\delta)} \ & \leq O\Big(\omega \sqrt{Ld}BR\cdot B\Big) = O ig(\omega \sqrt{Ld}B^2R ig). \end{align*} Choosing $\omega = o(1/(NL^2d^{2.5}B^3))$ as in Definition~ef{def:gd}, this is bounded by $O(R/(Bd\sqrt{Ld}))$, which is dominated by $R$. We therefore get $\| \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t) -\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0) \|_2 \leq O(R)$ for all $\ell \in [\ell]$ and $\|\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t) -\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0)\|_\infty \leq O(R/\sqrt{d})$. When $
u=2$, we have:  egin{align*} & ~ \|\sigma_{(2), p} (t) - \sigma_{(2), p} (0) \|_2 \ \leq & ~ O(1) \cdot \| \Lambda_{(1), i}(t) U_{(2)}(t)^	op \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t) - \Lambda_{(1), i}(0) U_{(2)}(0)^	op \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0) \|_2 \ = & ~ O(1) \cdot \| (\Lambda_{(1), i}(t) \otimes \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t))^	op \mathrm{vec}( U_{(2)}(t)) - (\Lambda_{(1), i}(0) \otimes \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0))^	op \mathrm{vec}( U_{(2)}(0))\|_2 \ \leq & ~ O(1) \cdot \Big( \|\Lambda_{(1), i}(t) \otimes \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t)\|_F \cdot O(R) \ & ~ \quad\quad ~~~~~~~~~~~~+\| U_{(2)}(0) \|_F \cdot \| \Lambda_{(1), i}(t) \otimes \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t) - \Lambda_{(1), i}(0) \otimes \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0)\|_F\Big) \ \leq & ~ O(\sqrt{L}R) \end{align*} where the first step follows from simple algebra and Fact~ef{fac:lipschitz_softmax}, the second step follows from a basic tensor trick, the third step follows from the {\it sum} form of the triangle inequality $\|AB - A'B'\|_F \le \|A-A'\|_F \|B\|_F + \|A'\|_F \|B-B'\|_F$ together with Part 4 of this lemma and $\|\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t) -\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0)\|_\infty \leq O(R/(Bd\sqrt{Ld}))$. Hence, we have:  egin{align*} \| o_{(2), i}(t) - o_{(2), i}(0) \|_2 = & ~ \| \Lambda_{(1), i}(t)^	op \sigma_{(2), p}(t) - \Lambda_{(1), i}(0)^	op \sigma_{(2), p}(0) \|_2 \ \leq & ~ \| \Lambda_{(1), i}(t) - \Lambda_{(1), i}(0)\|_F \cdot \|\sigma_{(2),p}(t)\|_2 + \| \Lambda_{(1), i}(0)\|_{m op} \cdot \|\sigma_{(2),p}(t)-\sigma_{(2),p}(0)\|_2 \ \leq & ~ O(\sqrt L R)\cdot O(1) + O(1)\cdot O(\sqrt{L}R) \ \leq & ~ O(\sqrt{L}R), \end{align*} where these steps follow from the {\it sum} triangle inequality $\|AB-A'B'\|\le \|A-A'\|\|B\| + \|A'\|\|B-B'\|$, Fact~ef{fac:lipschitz_softmax} for the softmax bound, and Part 10 of this Lemma. To extend $\|\Lambda_{(2),i,\ell}(t)-\Lambda_{(2),i,\ell}(0)\|_2$ from a $
u=2$-specific bound to the inductive step, we apply the same two-step argument as in Part~5. At $t=0$, $a_{(2),r,k}(0)\in\{-1,+1\}$ is i.i.d.\ uniform and independent of $w_{(2),r}(0)$, so Hoeffding's inequality (Lemma~ef{lem:hoeffding}) bounds the i.i.d.\ component as $O(\sqrt{m}\sqrt{d}B^2)$ with high probability; for $t>0$, the difference $\Lambda_{(2),i,\ell}(t)-\Lambda_{(2),i,\ell}(0)$ contains contributions from $w_{(2)}$, $U_{(2)}$, $A_{(2)}$ drift, each bounded by $R$, $R$, $R_A$ respectively (from Parts~9, 10 of this lemma and Lemma~ef{lem:ffn_drift}). The Lipschitz expansion in $(W, U, A)$ yields:  egin{align*} \|\Lambda_{(2),i,\ell}(t)-\Lambda_{(2),i,\ell}(0)\|_2 \le O(\sqrt L R) + O(\omega \sqrt d B \cdot R_A) = O(\sqrt L R), \end{align*} where the second equality uses the strengthened width condition of Lemma~ef{lem:ffn_drift} so that the $A$-drift term is dominated by the $W,U$-drift. By induction (using the same two-step Hoeffding-then-perturb argument at each layer), we obtain the bounds of Parts~11, 12, and 13. { f Proof of Part 14.} We have:  egin{align*} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D}) = & ~  rac{1}{n} \| {\sf F}(t) - {\sf Y} \|_F^2 \ \leq & ~ L\max_{p \in [nL]} \| {\sf F}_p(t) - {\sf Y}_p \|_2^2 \ \leq & ~ L\max_{p \in [nL]} \left( \| {\sf F}_p(t)\|_2 + \| {\sf Y}_p \|_2 ight)^2 \ \leq & ~ L \left( O(1) + O(\sqrt{d}) ight)^2 \ \leq & ~ O(Ld), \end{align*} where the first step follows from Lemma~ef{lem:compact_form_transform}, the second step follows from simple algebras, the third step follows from the Cauchy-Schwartz inequality, the last two steps follow from Definition~ef{def:D} and simple algebras. { f Proof of Part 15.} We show that $\| rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t,\mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d}\mu_{(
u)}(t)}\|_F^2 \asymp  rac{\varepsilon^2}{n} \cdot {\cal L}(t,\mathbb{D})$ by reverse induction on $
u$ from $N$ down to $1$. The $1/n$ factor in the bound is essential and traceable to the $1/n$ in the definition $\mathcal{L} =  rac{1}{n}\|\mathsf{F}-\mathsf{Y}\|_F^2$ of the average training loss (see the base case below). {\it Base case: $
u = N$.} By Part 3 of Lemma~ef{lem:grad_computation}, $ rac{\mathrm{d}{\cal L}(t,\mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mu_{(N), p}(t)} =  rac{2\varepsilon}{n}({\sf F}_p(t)-{\sf Y}_p)$ since $G_{(N),p}(t) = { f 0}_d$. Hence:  egin{align*} \Big\| rac{\mathrm{d}{\cal L}(t,\mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mu_{(N)}(t)}\Big\|_F^2 =  rac{4\varepsilon^2}{n^2}\sum_p \|{\sf F}_p(t)-{\sf Y}_p\|_2^2 =  rac{4\varepsilon^2}{n}\cdot {\cal L}(t,\mathbb{D}), \end{align*} using $\sum_p \|\mathsf{F}_p-\mathsf{Y}_p\|_2^2 = n\,\mathcal{L}(t,\mathbb{D})$ from Lemma~ef{lem:compact_form_transform}. This establishes $\| rac{\mathrm{d}{\cal L}}{\mathrm{d}\mu_{(N)}}\|_F^2 \le 4\varepsilon^2 \mathcal{L}/n \le O(\varepsilon^2 Ld/n)$ via Part~14, hence $\| rac{\mathrm{d}{\cal L}}{\mathrm{d}\mu_{(N)}}\|_F \le O(\varepsilon\sqrt{Ld/n})$. {\it Inductive step.} Assume the claim for layer $
u+1$. We bound the auxiliary term $G_{(
u),p}(t)$ (Part~3 of Lemma~ef{lem:grad_computation}). The factor $\kappa U_{(
u)}(t) \Lambda_{(
u-1),i}(t)^	op \mathrm{diag}({ f 1}_n -  rac{1}{2}e_\ell) (\mathrm{diag}\sigma - \sigma\sigma^	op)\Lambda_{(
u-1),i}(t)$ is bounded by:  egin{align*} & ~  ig\| \kappa U_{(
u)}(t)\Lambda_{(
u-1), i }(t)^	op \mathrm{diag}({ f 1}_n - 	frac{1}{2}e_\ell) (\mathrm{diag}\sigma_{(
u), p}(t) - \sigma_{(
u), p}(t)\sigma_{(
u), p}(t)^	op)\Lambda_{(
u-1), i }(t)  ig\|_F \ \leq & ~ \kappa \cdot \|U_{(
u)}(t)\|_F \cdot \|\Lambda_{(
u-1),i}(t)\|_F^2 \cdot O(1) \ \leq & ~ \kappa \cdot O(dB) \cdot O(L) \cdot O(1) \ = & ~ O(\kappa L^2dB) \leq O(L^2dB), \end{align*} where we use Parts 4 and 5, the fact that $\mathrm{diag}\sigma - \sigma\sigma^	op$ has spectral norm at most $1$, and $\kappa = 1/\sqrt{m} \leq 1$. To bound the random sum $\sum_{r\in[m]} a_{(
u),r}(t)\langle rac{\mathrm{d}{\cal L}}{\mathrm{d}\mu_{(
u+1),p}}, a_{(
u),r}(t)angle\, w_{(
u),r}(t)\,\mathbb{I}\{\cdot\}$, we again apply Hoeffding {\it at $t=0$} (where $a_{(
u),r,k}(0)\in\{-1,+1\}$ is i.i.d.\ and independent of $w_{(
u),r}(0)$) to obtain $\|G_{(
u),p}(0)\|_2^2 \le \omega\cdot O(L^2 d^{2.5} B^3)$, and then propagate to $t>0$ via the $A$-drift bound $\|A_{(
u)}(t)-A_{(
u)}(0)\|_F \le R_A$ from Lemma~ef{lem:ffn_drift} and the $W$-drift bound $\|w_{(
u),r}(t)-w_{(
u),r}(0)\|_2 \le R$ from Part~9 of this lemma:  egin{align*} \|G_{(
u),p}(t)\|_2 \le \|G_{(
u),p}(0)\|_2 + O(\omega\sqrt{m}\,\|A_{(
u)}(t)-A_{(
u)}(0)\|_F + \omega\sqrt{m d}\,R) = O(\sqrt\omega \cdot Ld^{1.25}B^{1.5}), \end{align*} so that $\|G_{(
u),p}(t)\|_2^2 \le \omega\cdot O(L^2 d^{2.5}B^3) \le o(1)$ under Definition~ef{def:gd}'s choice $\omega = o(1/(NL^2 d^{2.5}B^3))$ and the strengthened width of Lemma~ef{lem:ffn_drift}. Therefore $I_d + \mathrm{diag}(G_{(
u),p}(t)) = (1\pm o(1))I_d$, and by Part~3 of Lemma~ef{lem:grad_computation}:  egin{align*} \Big\| rac{\mathrm{d}{\cal L}}{\mathrm{d}\mu_{(
u),p}(t)}\Big\|_2 =  rac{2\varepsilon}{n}\|({\sf F}_p(t)-{\sf Y}_p)\|_2(1\pm o(1)), \end{align*} which preserves the $\Theta(\varepsilon^2{\cal L}/n)$ per-layer scaling. Summing over $p\in[nL]$ (which produces a single factor of $n$ from $\sum_p \|\mathsf{F}_p-\mathsf{Y}_p\|^2 = n\mathcal{L}$) and inducting:  egin{align*}  ig\|  rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mu_{(
u)}(t)}  ig\|_F^2 \asymp  rac{\varepsilon^2}{n} \cdot {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D}). \end{align*} { f Proof of Part 16.} We bound $\|\gamma_{(
u),p}(t)\|_2$, where $\gamma_{(
u),p}(t)$ is the kernel feature for $U_{(
u)}$. By the definition, the leading factor is $ rac{\omega \kappa}{\sqrt{m}}$, multiplied by tensors of bounded norm (Part~5, Part~7) and a sum over $r$ that is controlled by Hoeffding as in Part~15. Choosing $\kappa = 1/\sqrt{m}$ as in Definition~ef{def:gd}, we have $ rac{\omega\kappa}{\sqrt{m}} =  rac{\omega}{m}$, and the entire bound reduces to $\| \gamma_{(
u),p}(t)\|_2 \leq o(1/\sqrt{m})$, completing the proof. This completes the proof of all parts of the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Part by part: Gaussian tails and union bounds, triangle inequalities, Hoeffding at initialization then Lipschitz perturbation, and induction over layers. Part 5 bootstraps through the FFN-drift lemma.

nodes.name: Part 1
nodes.statement:
{ f Proof of Part 1.} Each entry $w_{(
u),r,k}(0)$ is i.i.d.\ $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ by initialization. By Fact~ef{fac:gaussian_tail}, $|w_{(
u),r,k}(0)| \le C\sqrt{\log(Nmd/\delta)}$ with probability at least $1 - \delta/(Nmd)$. A union bound over $
u\in[N], r\in[m], k\in[d]$ shows that all entries are bounded by $C\sqrt{\log(Nmd/\delta)}$ simultaneously with probability at least $1-\delta$. Thus $\|w_{(
u),r}(0)\|_2^2 = \sum_{k\in[d]} w_{(
u),r,k}(0)^2 \le d \cdot C^2\log(Nmd/\delta) = O(d B^2)$, giving $\|w_{(
u),r}(0)\|_2 \le O(\sqrt d B)$.
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian tail plus union bound

nodes.name: Part 2
nodes.statement:
{ f Proof of Part 2.} Analogously, each entry $U_{(
u),k_1,k_2}(0)$ is i.i.d.\ $\mathcal{N}(0,1)$. By Fact~ef{fac:gaussian_tail} and a union bound over $
u\in[N], (k_1,k_2)\in[d]	imes[d]$, all entries are bounded by $O(B)$ with probability at least $1-\delta$. Therefore $\|U_{(
u)}(0)\|_F^2 = \sum_{k_1,k_2} U_{(
u),k_1,k_2}(0)^2 \le d^2\cdot O(B^2) = O(d^2 B^2)$, hence $\|U_{(
u)}(0)\|_F \le O(dB)$.
nodes.statement_short: Same for $U(0)$

nodes.name: Part 3
nodes.statement:
{ f Proof of Part 3.} By triangle inequality, $\|w_{(
u),r}(t)\|_2 \le \|w_{(
u),r}(0)\|_2 + \|w_{(
u),r}(t)-w_{(
u),r}(0)\|_2 \le O(\sqrt dB) + R$ from Part~1 and the lemma's hypothesis. Since $R \in (0,1)$ and $B\ge 1$ (so $\sqrt d B\ge 1$), the second summand is dominated and $\|w_{(
u),r}(t)\|_2 \le O(\sqrt d B)$.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality with the drift hypothesis

nodes.name: Part 4
nodes.statement:
{ f Proof of Part 4.} Analogously to Part~3, $\|U_{(
u)}(t)\|_F \le \|U_{(
u)}(0)\|_F + \|U_{(
u)}(t)-U_{(
u)}(0)\|_F \le O(dB) + R$, and the second summand is dominated by the first under $R\in(0,1)$ and $B\ge 1$, giving $\|U_{(
u)}(t)\|_F \le O(dB)$.
nodes.statement_short: Same for $U(t)$

nodes.name: Part 5
nodes.statement_short: Hidden states stay $\Theta(1)$: Hoeffding at $t=0$, perturbation for $t>0$, induction over layers

nodes.name: Two-step plan
nodes.statement:
{ f Proof of Part 5.} Because $A_{(
u)}$ is trained jointly with $W_{(
u)},U_{(
u)}$ by gradient flow (Section~ef{sec:preli}), the entries $a_{(
u),r,k}(t)$ are no longer in $\{-1,+1\}$ for $t>0$ and are in general not independent of $w_{(
u),r}(t)$. We therefore prove Part~5 in two steps: first at the initialization time $t=0$ via Hoeffding (where the i.i.d.\ $\pm 1$ assumption holds), then for $t>0$ via the perturbation bound of Part~13 of this lemma and the FFN-drift bound of Lemma~ef{lem:ffn_drift}.
nodes.statement_short: Prove at $t=0$ by Hoeffding, then extend via drift bounds

nodes.name: Step 1
nodes.statement_short: Layer 1 at initialization via Hoeffding

nodes.name: Step 2
nodes.statement_short: Extend to $t>0$ with $W$, $o$ and $A$ drift bounds

nodes.name: Step 3
nodes.statement:
{\it Step 3: Inductive step ($
u \ge 2$).} Assume the bound holds for layer $
u-1$. Then $\|\Lambda_{(
u-1),i,\ell}(t)\|_2 = \Theta(1)$ uniformly in $\ell$ and $t$, hence $\|o_{(
u),p}(t)\|_2 = \|\Lambda_{(
u-1),i}(t)^	op\sigma_{(
u),p}(t)\|_2 \le \max_{\ell'}\|\Lambda_{(
u-1),i,\ell'}(t)\|_2 = \Theta(1)$. The Hoeffding-then-perturb argument of Steps~1 and~2 applies verbatim to $\mu_{(
u),p}$ (with all quantities re-indexed to layer $
u$), giving $\|\Lambda_{(
u),i,\ell}(t)\|_2 = \Theta(1)$ as claimed. The bound on $\|o_{(
u),p}(t)\|_2$ follows directly:
     egin{align} \|o_{(
u), p}(t)\|_2 = \Theta(1).
    \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Inductive step over layers

nodes.name: Part 6
nodes.statement:
{\bf Proof of Part 6.} We have:
    \begin{align*}
        \| \Lambda_{(\nu), i}(t) U_{(\nu)}(t) \Lambda_{(\nu), i}(t)^\top \|_\infty 
        = & ~ \max_{(\ell_1, \ell_2) \in [L] \times [L]}  \left| \Lambda_{(\nu), i, \ell_1}(t)^\top U_{(\nu)}(t) \Lambda_{(\nu), i, \ell_2}(t) \right| \\
        \leq & ~ O(dB)
    \end{align*}
    where the first step follows from simple algebra, the second step follows from Part 4 and Part 5 of this lemma and Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz with Parts 4 and 5

nodes.name: Part 7
nodes.statement:
{ f Proof of Part 7.} From Part~6, $\|\Lambda_{(
u),i}(t) U_{(
u)}(t) \Lambda_{(
u),i}(t)^	op\|_\infty \le O(dB)$, so each attention logit $z_{p,\ell'} :=  ig[\Lambda_{(
u),i}(t) U_{(
u)}(t) \Lambda_{(
u),i}(t)^	op ig]_{\ell, \ell'}$ satisfies $|z_{p,\ell'}| \le O(dB)$. Therefore $\exp(z_{p,\ell'}) \in [\exp(-O(dB)), \exp(O(dB))]$, which is the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Exponentiate the logit bound

nodes.name: Part 8
nodes.statement_short: Lower-bound softmax entries

nodes.name: Part 9
nodes.statement: {\bf Proof of Part 9.} This is a direct restatement of the lemma's hypothesis $\|w_{(\nu),r}(t) - w_{(\nu),r}(0)\|_2 \le R$, which is a bootstrapping assumption that is verified self-consistently in Lemma~\ref{lem:perturbations} (where we prove that the gradient flow keeps the iterates inside this ball).
nodes.statement_short: Restates the drift hypothesis

nodes.name: Part 10
nodes.statement: {\bf Proof of Part 10.} Likewise, this is a direct restatement of the hypothesis $\|U_{(\nu)}(t) - U_{(\nu)}(0)\|_F \le R$, verified self-consistently in Lemma~\ref{lem:perturbations}.
nodes.statement_short: Restates the $U$-drift hypothesis

nodes.name: Parts 11-13
nodes.statement:
{\bf Proof of Part 11, 12 and 13.} We proceed by induction on the layer index $\nu$. The base case $\nu=0$ is trivial since $\Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(t) = X_{i,\ell} + E_\ell$ does not depend on $t$, and so $\Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(t) = \Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(0)$.

    {\it Base case: $\nu=1$.} By the definition of $\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t)$ as the $\ell$-th token of layer-1 output:
    \begin{align*}
        & ~ \| \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t) -\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0)\|_2 \\
        = & ~ \sqrt{\sum_{k\in [d]} \left(\frac{\omega}{\sqrt{m}} \cdot \sum_{r=1}^m a_{(1), r, k} \left(\phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(t), o_{(1), p}(t) \rangle) - \phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(0), o_{(1), p}(0) \rangle) \right) \right)^2 },
    \end{align*}
    where the residual connection contributes $\Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(t) - \Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(0) = 0$ and the difference reduces to the FFN-after-attention contribution.

    We first bound $\|\sigma_{(1),p}(t)-\sigma_{(1),p}(0)\|_2$ via softmax Lipschitzness. Note that $\sigma_{(1),p}(t)$ is a function of the attention logits $\Lambda_{(0), i}(0) U_{(1)}(t)^\top \Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(0) \in \mathbb{R}^L$ (here $\Lambda_{(0), i}(t)=\Lambda_{(0), i}(0)$ is fixed). Hence:
    \begin{align*}
        \| \sigma_{(1), p}(t) - \sigma_{(1), p}(0) \|_2
        \leq & ~ O(1) \cdot \| \Lambda_{(0), i}(0) ( U_{(1)}(t) - U_{(1)}(0) )^\top \Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(0) \|_2 \\
        \leq & ~ O(1) \cdot \|\Lambda_{(0), i}(0)\|_F \cdot \| U_{(1)}(t) - U_{(1)}(0) \|_F \cdot \| \Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(0) \|_2 \\
        \leq & ~ O(1) \cdot O(\sqrt{L}) \cdot R \cdot O(1) = O(\sqrt{L}R),
    \end{align*}
    where the first step follows from the definition of $\sigma_{(1), p}(t)$ and Fact~\ref{fac:lipschitz_softmax}, the second step from operator-norm submultiplicativity (Cauchy--Schwarz on a quadratic form), the third step from $\|\Lambda_{(0), i}(0)\|_F = O(\sqrt{L})$ (since each token has unit norm, summed over $L$ tokens), $\|U_{(1)}(t) - U_{(1)}(0)\|_F \le R$ (Part 10), and $\|\Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(0)\|_2 = O(1)$.

    Next, we use the identity $o_{(1),p}(t) = \Lambda_{(0), i}(0)^\top \sigma_{(1), p}(t)$ together with the operator-norm bound $\|\Lambda_{(0),i}(0)\|_{\rm op} = O(1)$ that follows from the per-token unit-norm constraint $\|X_\ell\|_2 = \Theta(1)$ (Section~\ref{sub:setups}) under the residual-and-RMSNorm structure:
    \begin{align*}
        \| o_{(1), p}(t) - o_{(1), p}(0) \|_2 = & ~ \| \Lambda_{(0), i}(0)^\top \big( \sigma_{(1), p}(t) - \sigma_{(1), p}(0) \big) \|_2 \\
        \leq & ~ \|\Lambda_{(0), i}(0)\|_{\rm op} \cdot \| \sigma_{(1), p}(t) - \sigma_{(1), p}(0) \|_2 \\
        \leq & ~ O(1) \cdot O(\sqrt{L}R) = O(\sqrt{L} R),
    \end{align*}
    which matches Part~13.

    For a fixed index $k \in [d]$, we apply Hoeffding's inequality (Lemma~\ref{lem:hoeffding}) to the random variables $a_{(1), r, k} \cdot \big(\phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(t), o_{(1), p}(t) \rangle) - \phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(0), o_{(1), p}(0) \rangle)\big)$ for $r \in [m]$. By Fact~\ref{fac:lipschitz_1} (the ReLU $\phi$ is $1$-Lipschitz):
    \begin{align*}
        & ~ \big| a_{(1), r, k} \cdot \big(\phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(t), o_{(1), p}(t) \rangle) - \phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(0), o_{(1), p}(0) \rangle)\big) \big| \\
        \leq & ~ |a_{(1), r, k}| \cdot \big| \langle w_{(1), r}(t), o_{(1), p}(t) \rangle - \langle w_{(1), r}(0), o_{(1), p}(0) \rangle \big| \\
        \leq & ~ 1 \cdot \big( \| w_{(1), r}(t) - w_{(1), r}(0) \|_2 \cdot \| o_{(1), p}(t) \|_2 + \| w_{(1), r}(0) \|_2 \cdot \| o_{(1), p}(t) - o_{(1), p}(0) \|_2 \big) \\
        \leq & ~ R \cdot O(1) + O(\sqrt{d} B) \cdot O(\sqrt{L} R) \\
        \leq & ~ O(\sqrt{Ld}BR),
    \end{align*}
    where the second step follows from $|a_{(1),r,k}|=1$ and the bilinear difference identity, the third step from the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality together with the perturbation bounds Part 9 and Part 13 of this lemma, the fourth step from $\|w_{(1),r}(0)\|_2\leq O(\sqrt{d}B)$ (Part 1) and $\|o_{(1),p}(t)\|_2 = O(1)$. The mean is zero since $a_{(1), r, k} \in \{-1,+1\}$ uniformly and is independent of $w$:
    \begin{align*}
         {\mathbb{E}}\big[a_{(1), r, k} \cdot \big( \phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(t), o_{(1), p}(t) \rangle) - \phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(0), o_{(1), p}(0) \rangle)\big)\big] =  0.
    \end{align*}
    By Lemma~\ref{lem:hoeffding}, for any fixed $k$, with probability at least $1 - \delta/(md)$:
    \begin{align*}
        &  ~ \Big| \frac{\omega}{\sqrt{m}} \sum_{r=1}^m a_{(1), r, k} \cdot \big(\phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(t), o_{(1), p}(t) \rangle) - \phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(0), o_{(1), p}(0) \rangle)\big) \Big| \\
        & \leq \frac{\omega}{\sqrt{m}}\cdot O(\sqrt{Ld}BR)\cdot\sqrt{m\log(md/\delta)} \\
        & \leq O\Big(\omega \sqrt{Ld}BR\cdot B\Big) = O\big(\omega \sqrt{Ld}B^2R\big).
    \end{align*}
    Choosing $\omega = o(1/(NL^2d^{2.5}B^3))$ as in Definition~\ref{def:gd}, this is bounded by $O(R/(Bd\sqrt{Ld}))$, which is dominated by $R$.

    We therefore get $\| \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t) -\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0)  \|_2 \leq O(R)$ for all $\ell \in [\ell]$ and $\|\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t) -\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0)\|_\infty \leq O(R/\sqrt{d})$.

    When $\nu=2$, we have:
    \begin{align*}
        & ~ \|\sigma_{(2), p} (t) - \sigma_{(2), p} (0) \|_2 \\
        \leq & ~ O(1) \cdot \| \Lambda_{(1), i}(t) U_{(2)}(t)^\top  \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t)  - \Lambda_{(1), i}(0) U_{(2)}(0)^\top  \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0) \|_2 \\
        = & ~ O(1) \cdot \| (\Lambda_{(1), i}(t) \otimes \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t))^\top \mathrm{vec}( U_{(2)}(t)) - (\Lambda_{(1), i}(0) \otimes \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0))^\top \mathrm{vec}( U_{(2)}(0))\|_2 \\
        \leq & ~ O(1) \cdot \Big( \|\Lambda_{(1), i}(t) \otimes \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t)\|_F \cdot O(R) \\
        & ~ \quad\quad ~~~~~~~~~~~~+\| U_{(2)}(0) \|_F \cdot \| \Lambda_{(1), i}(t) \otimes \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t) - \Lambda_{(1), i}(0) \otimes \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0)\|_F\Big) \\
        \leq & ~ O(\sqrt{L}R)
    \end{align*}
    where the first step follows from simple algebra and Fact~\ref{fac:lipschitz_softmax}, the second step follows from a basic tensor trick, the third step follows from the {\it sum} form of the triangle inequality $\|AB - A'B'\|_F \le \|A-A'\|_F \|B\|_F + \|A'\|_F \|B-B'\|_F$ together with Part 4 of this lemma and $\|\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t) -\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0)\|_\infty \leq O(R/(Bd\sqrt{Ld}))$.

    Hence, we have:
    \begin{align*}
        \| o_{(2), i}(t) - o_{(2), i}(0) \|_2 = & ~ \| \Lambda_{(1), i}(t)^\top \sigma_{(2), p}(t) - \Lambda_{(1), i}(0)^\top \sigma_{(2), p}(0) \|_2 \\
        \leq & ~ \| \Lambda_{(1), i}(t) - \Lambda_{(1), i}(0)\|_F \cdot \|\sigma_{(2),p}(t)\|_2 + \| \Lambda_{(1), i}(0)\|_{\rm op} \cdot \|\sigma_{(2),p}(t)-\sigma_{(2),p}(0)\|_2 \\
        \leq & ~ O(\sqrt L R)\cdot O(1) + O(1)\cdot O(\sqrt{L}R) \\
        \leq & ~ O(\sqrt{L}R),
    \end{align*}
    where these steps follow from the {\it sum} triangle inequality $\|AB-A'B'\|\le \|A-A'\|\|B\| + \|A'\|\|B-B'\|$, Fact~\ref{fac:lipschitz_softmax} for the softmax bound, and Part 10 of this Lemma.

    To extend $\|\Lambda_{(2),i,\ell}(t)-\Lambda_{(2),i,\ell}(0)\|_2$ from a $\nu=2$-specific bound to the inductive step, we apply the same two-step argument as in Part~5. At $t=0$, $a_{(2),r,k}(0)\in\{-1,+1\}$ is i.i.d.\ uniform and independent of $w_{(2),r}(0)$, so Hoeffding's inequality (Lemma~\ref{lem:hoeffding}) bounds the i.i.d.\ component as $O(\sqrt{m}\sqrt{d}B^2)$ with high probability; for $t>0$, the difference $\Lambda_{(2),i,\ell}(t)-\Lambda_{(2),i,\ell}(0)$ contains contributions from $w_{(2)}$, $U_{(2)}$, $A_{(2)}$ drift, each bounded by $R$, $R$, $R_A$ respectively (from Parts~9, 10 of this lemma and Lemma~\ref{lem:ffn_drift}). The Lipschitz expansion in $(W, U, A)$ yields:
    \begin{align*}
        \|\Lambda_{(2),i,\ell}(t)-\Lambda_{(2),i,\ell}(0)\|_2 \le O(\sqrt L R) + O(\omega \sqrt d B \cdot R_A) = O(\sqrt L R),
    \end{align*}
    where the second equality uses the strengthened width condition of Lemma~\ref{lem:ffn_drift} so that the $A$-drift term is dominated by the $W,U$-drift.

    By induction (using the same two-step Hoeffding-then-perturb argument at each layer), we obtain the bounds of Parts~11, 12, and 13.
nodes.statement_short: Induction over layers on drift of hidden states, scores and attention outputs

nodes.name: Induction setup
nodes.statement: {\bf Proof of Part 11, 12 and 13.} We proceed by induction on the layer index $\nu$. The base case $\nu=0$ is trivial since $\Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(t) = X_{i,\ell} + E_\ell$ does not depend on $t$, and so $\Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(t) = \Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(0)$.
nodes.statement_short: Induct on layers; $\nu=0$ is trivial

nodes.name: Base case
nodes.statement:
{\it Base case: $\nu=1$.} By the definition of $\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t)$ as the $\ell$-th token of layer-1 output:
    \begin{align*}
        & ~ \| \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t) -\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0)\|_2 \\
        = & ~ \sqrt{\sum_{k\in [d]} \left(\frac{\omega}{\sqrt{m}} \cdot \sum_{r=1}^m a_{(1), r, k} \left(\phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(t), o_{(1), p}(t) \rangle) - \phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(0), o_{(1), p}(0) \rangle) \right) \right)^2 },
    \end{align*}
    where the residual connection contributes $\Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(t) - \Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(0) = 0$ and the difference reduces to the FFN-after-attention contribution.

    We first bound $\|\sigma_{(1),p}(t)-\sigma_{(1),p}(0)\|_2$ via softmax Lipschitzness. Note that $\sigma_{(1),p}(t)$ is a function of the attention logits $\Lambda_{(0), i}(0) U_{(1)}(t)^\top \Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(0) \in \mathbb{R}^L$ (here $\Lambda_{(0), i}(t)=\Lambda_{(0), i}(0)$ is fixed). Hence:
    \begin{align*}
        \| \sigma_{(1), p}(t) - \sigma_{(1), p}(0) \|_2
        \leq & ~ O(1) \cdot \| \Lambda_{(0), i}(0) ( U_{(1)}(t) - U_{(1)}(0) )^\top \Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(0) \|_2 \\
        \leq & ~ O(1) \cdot \|\Lambda_{(0), i}(0)\|_F \cdot \| U_{(1)}(t) - U_{(1)}(0) \|_F \cdot \| \Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(0) \|_2 \\
        \leq & ~ O(1) \cdot O(\sqrt{L}) \cdot R \cdot O(1) = O(\sqrt{L}R),
    \end{align*}
    where the first step follows from the definition of $\sigma_{(1), p}(t)$ and Fact~\ref{fac:lipschitz_softmax}, the second step from operator-norm submultiplicativity (Cauchy--Schwarz on a quadratic form), the third step from $\|\Lambda_{(0), i}(0)\|_F = O(\sqrt{L})$ (since each token has unit norm, summed over $L$ tokens), $\|U_{(1)}(t) - U_{(1)}(0)\|_F \le R$ (Part 10), and $\|\Lambda_{(0), i, \ell}(0)\|_2 = O(1)$.

    Next, we use the identity $o_{(1),p}(t) = \Lambda_{(0), i}(0)^\top \sigma_{(1), p}(t)$ together with the operator-norm bound $\|\Lambda_{(0),i}(0)\|_{\rm op} = O(1)$ that follows from the per-token unit-norm constraint $\|X_\ell\|_2 = \Theta(1)$ (Section~\ref{sub:setups}) under the residual-and-RMSNorm structure:
    \begin{align*}
        \| o_{(1), p}(t) - o_{(1), p}(0) \|_2 = & ~ \| \Lambda_{(0), i}(0)^\top \big( \sigma_{(1), p}(t) - \sigma_{(1), p}(0) \big) \|_2 \\
        \leq & ~ \|\Lambda_{(0), i}(0)\|_{\rm op} \cdot \| \sigma_{(1), p}(t) - \sigma_{(1), p}(0) \|_2 \\
        \leq & ~ O(1) \cdot O(\sqrt{L}R) = O(\sqrt{L} R),
    \end{align*}
    which matches Part~13.

    For a fixed index $k \in [d]$, we apply Hoeffding's inequality (Lemma~\ref{lem:hoeffding}) to the random variables $a_{(1), r, k} \cdot \big(\phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(t), o_{(1), p}(t) \rangle) - \phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(0), o_{(1), p}(0) \rangle)\big)$ for $r \in [m]$. By Fact~\ref{fac:lipschitz_1} (the ReLU $\phi$ is $1$-Lipschitz):
    \begin{align*}
        & ~ \big| a_{(1), r, k} \cdot \big(\phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(t), o_{(1), p}(t) \rangle) - \phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(0), o_{(1), p}(0) \rangle)\big) \big| \\
        \leq & ~ |a_{(1), r, k}| \cdot \big| \langle w_{(1), r}(t), o_{(1), p}(t) \rangle - \langle w_{(1), r}(0), o_{(1), p}(0) \rangle \big| \\
        \leq & ~ 1 \cdot \big( \| w_{(1), r}(t) - w_{(1), r}(0) \|_2 \cdot \| o_{(1), p}(t) \|_2 + \| w_{(1), r}(0) \|_2 \cdot \| o_{(1), p}(t) - o_{(1), p}(0) \|_2 \big) \\
        \leq & ~ R \cdot O(1) + O(\sqrt{d} B) \cdot O(\sqrt{L} R) \\
        \leq & ~ O(\sqrt{Ld}BR),
    \end{align*}
    where the second step follows from $|a_{(1),r,k}|=1$ and the bilinear difference identity, the third step from the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality together with the perturbation bounds Part 9 and Part 13 of this lemma, the fourth step from $\|w_{(1),r}(0)\|_2\leq O(\sqrt{d}B)$ (Part 1) and $\|o_{(1),p}(t)\|_2 = O(1)$. The mean is zero since $a_{(1), r, k} \in \{-1,+1\}$ uniformly and is independent of $w$:
    \begin{align*}
         {\mathbb{E}}\big[a_{(1), r, k} \cdot \big( \phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(t), o_{(1), p}(t) \rangle) - \phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(0), o_{(1), p}(0) \rangle)\big)\big] =  0.
    \end{align*}
    By Lemma~\ref{lem:hoeffding}, for any fixed $k$, with probability at least $1 - \delta/(md)$:
    \begin{align*}
        &  ~ \Big| \frac{\omega}{\sqrt{m}} \sum_{r=1}^m a_{(1), r, k} \cdot \big(\phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(t), o_{(1), p}(t) \rangle) - \phi(\langle w_{(1), r}(0), o_{(1), p}(0) \rangle)\big) \Big| \\
        & \leq \frac{\omega}{\sqrt{m}}\cdot O(\sqrt{Ld}BR)\cdot\sqrt{m\log(md/\delta)} \\
        & \leq O\Big(\omega \sqrt{Ld}BR\cdot B\Big) = O\big(\omega \sqrt{Ld}B^2R\big).
    \end{align*}
    Choosing $\omega = o(1/(NL^2d^{2.5}B^3))$ as in Definition~\ref{def:gd}, this is bounded by $O(R/(Bd\sqrt{Ld}))$, which is dominated by $R$.

    We therefore get $\| \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t) -\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0)  \|_2 \leq O(R)$ for all $\ell \in [\ell]$ and $\|\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t) -\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0)\|_\infty \leq O(R/\sqrt{d})$.
nodes.statement_short: Layer 1: softmax Lipschitzness, then Hoeffding on the FFN difference

nodes.name: Layer 2
nodes.statement:
When $\nu=2$, we have:
    \begin{align*}
        & ~ \|\sigma_{(2), p} (t) - \sigma_{(2), p} (0) \|_2 \\
        \leq & ~ O(1) \cdot \| \Lambda_{(1), i}(t) U_{(2)}(t)^\top  \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t)  - \Lambda_{(1), i}(0) U_{(2)}(0)^\top  \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0) \|_2 \\
        = & ~ O(1) \cdot \| (\Lambda_{(1), i}(t) \otimes \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t))^\top \mathrm{vec}( U_{(2)}(t)) - (\Lambda_{(1), i}(0) \otimes \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0))^\top \mathrm{vec}( U_{(2)}(0))\|_2 \\
        \leq & ~ O(1) \cdot \Big( \|\Lambda_{(1), i}(t) \otimes \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t)\|_F \cdot O(R) \\
        & ~ \quad\quad ~~~~~~~~~~~~+\| U_{(2)}(0) \|_F \cdot \| \Lambda_{(1), i}(t) \otimes \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t) - \Lambda_{(1), i}(0) \otimes \Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0)\|_F\Big) \\
        \leq & ~ O(\sqrt{L}R)
    \end{align*}
    where the first step follows from simple algebra and Fact~\ref{fac:lipschitz_softmax}, the second step follows from a basic tensor trick, the third step follows from the {\it sum} form of the triangle inequality $\|AB - A'B'\|_F \le \|A-A'\|_F \|B\|_F + \|A'\|_F \|B-B'\|_F$ together with Part 4 of this lemma and $\|\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(t) -\Lambda_{(1), i, \ell}(0)\|_\infty \leq O(R/(Bd\sqrt{Ld}))$.

    Hence, we have:
    \begin{align*}
        \| o_{(2), i}(t) - o_{(2), i}(0) \|_2 = & ~ \| \Lambda_{(1), i}(t)^\top \sigma_{(2), p}(t) - \Lambda_{(1), i}(0)^\top \sigma_{(2), p}(0) \|_2 \\
        \leq & ~ \| \Lambda_{(1), i}(t) - \Lambda_{(1), i}(0)\|_F \cdot \|\sigma_{(2),p}(t)\|_2 + \| \Lambda_{(1), i}(0)\|_{\rm op} \cdot \|\sigma_{(2),p}(t)-\sigma_{(2),p}(0)\|_2 \\
        \leq & ~ O(\sqrt L R)\cdot O(1) + O(1)\cdot O(\sqrt{L}R) \\
        \leq & ~ O(\sqrt{L}R),
    \end{align*}
    where these steps follow from the {\it sum} triangle inequality $\|AB-A'B'\|\le \|A-A'\|\|B\| + \|A'\|\|B-B'\|$, Fact~\ref{fac:lipschitz_softmax} for the softmax bound, and Part 10 of this Lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Layer 2 via the sum triangle inequality

nodes.name: Extension
nodes.statement_short: Hoeffding-then-perturb with the FFN drift

nodes.name: Induction
nodes.statement: By induction (using the same two-step Hoeffding-then-perturb argument at each layer), we obtain the bounds of Parts~11, 12, and 13.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude Parts 11-13 by induction

nodes.name: Part 14
nodes.statement_short: Bound the loss by $O(Ld)$

nodes.name: Part 15
nodes.statement:
{ f Proof of Part 15.}
    We show that $\| rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t,\mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d}\mu_{(
u)}(t)}\|_F^2 \asymp  rac{\varepsilon^2}{n} \cdot {\cal L}(t,\mathbb{D})$ by reverse induction on $
u$ from $N$ down to $1$. The $1/n$ factor in the bound is essential and traceable to the $1/n$ in the definition $\mathcal{L} =  rac{1}{n}\|\mathsf{F}-\mathsf{Y}\|_F^2$ of the average training loss (see the base case below).

u = N$.} By Part 3 of Lemma~ef{lem:grad_computation}, $ rac{\mathrm{d}{\cal L}(t,\mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mu_{(N), p}(t)} =  rac{2\varepsilon}{n}({\sf F}_p(t)-{\sf Y}_p)$ since $G_{(N),p}(t) = { f 0}_d$. Hence:

u+1$. We bound the auxiliary term $G_{(

    To bound the random sum $\sum_{r\in[m]} a_{(

    which preserves the $\Theta(\varepsilon^2{\cal L}/n)$ per-layer scaling. Summing over $p\in[nL]$ (which produces a single factor of $n$ from $\sum_p \|\mathsf{F}_p-\mathsf{Y}_p\|^2 = n\mathcal{L}$) and inducting:
     egin{align*}
         ig\|  rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} \mu_{(

nodes.statement:
{\bf Proof of Part 15.}
    We show that $\|\frac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t,\mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d}\mu_{(\nu)}(t)}\|_F^2 \asymp \frac{\varepsilon^2}{n} \cdot {\cal L}(t,\mathbb{D})$ by reverse induction on $\nu$ from $N$ down to $1$. The $1/n$ factor in the bound is essential and traceable to the $1/n$ in the definition $\mathcal{L} = \frac{1}{n}\|\mathsf{F}-\mathsf{Y}\|_F^2$ of the average training loss (see the base case below).

This establishes $\|\frac{\mathrm{d}{\cal L}}{\mathrm{d}\mu_{(N)}}\|_F^2 \le 4\varepsilon^2 \mathcal{L}/n \le O(\varepsilon^2 Ld/n)$ via Part~14, hence $\|\frac{\mathrm{d}{\cal L}}{\mathrm{d}\mu_{(N)}}\|_F \le O(\varepsilon\sqrt{Ld/n})$.

{ f Proof of Part 16.}
    We bound $\|\gamma_{(

nodes.statement_short: Attention feature norm is $o(1/\sqrt m)$ with $\kappa=1/\sqrt m$

nodes.name: On the non-parallelism condition (P2)
nodes.statement:
Condition (P2) is automatically satisfied, with high probability, in our setting: the inputs $X\in {\cal X}$ are RMSNormed so $\|X_\ell\|_2=\Theta(1)$ (Section~ef{sub:setups}); for $
u=1$, $o_{(1),p}(0)$ is a softmax-weighted convex combination of the input tokens, hence inherits non-parallelism from the input distribution. For $
u\ge 2$, $o_{(
u),p}(0)$ is the attention output of the previous layer, which is a generic non-degenerate function of $\{o_{(
u-1),p}(0)\}_p$; the only way (P2) fails is if a positive-measure subset of input sequences has identical layer-$
u$ representations, which is an event of measure zero under any continuous data distribution. We therefore treat Assumption~ef{ass:positive_definite} as a {\it consequence} of input non-degeneracy + the architecture, rather than an opaque assumption. A formal counterexample requires constructing an input distribution that places mass on ``collision'' configurations; we are not aware of any such pathology arising in practice.

nodes.statement_short: RMSNorm and continuous data make collisions of attention outputs a measure-zero event, so (P2) holds generically.

nodes.statement: Assuming Assumption~\ref{ass:positive_definite} and Definition~\ref{def:gd} hold, denote the failure probability $\delta \in (0, 0.1)$, then the kernel perturbation bound is: \begin{align*} \Pr\left[\lambda_{\min}(H_{(\nu)}(t)) < \omega\lambda /2\right] < \delta. \end{align*} Therefore, bounding loss dynamics is given by ($C > 0$ is an absolute constant): \begin{align*} \Pr\left[{\mathbb{E}}\!\left[\frac{\mathrm{d} }{\mathrm{d} t}{\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})\right] > - \frac{C \cdot \omega\lambda N \cdot \varepsilon^2}{n} \cdot {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})\right] < \delta. \end{align*} {\it (The $\varepsilon^2/n$ factor appears explicitly: $\varepsilon^2$ comes from Part~15 of Lemma~\ref{lem:helpful_bounds}, and the $1/n$ factor is the $1/n$ in $\mathcal{L} = \frac{1}{n}\|\mathsf{F}-\mathsf{Y}\|_F^2$. We track this $1/n$ explicitly because it propagates downstream into the phase-boundary exponent of Theorem~\ref{thm:scaling_law}.)}

u\in [N]} \| U_{(
u)}(T) - U_{(
u)}(0) \|_F \leq O( rac{1}{\sqrt{m} \omega\lambda N}) =: R \end{align*} { f Tighter Bound.} We plug $R = O( rac{1}{\sqrt{m} \omega\lambda N})$ and $N = O(1)$ into Equation~\eqref{eq:kernel_perturbation} to get:  egin{align*} \| H_{(
u)}'(t) - H_{(
u)}'(0) \|_F \leq & ~ O(nL^{1.5} rac{1}{\sqrt{m} \omega\lambda N}) \cdot \exp(O(dB)) /\delta \leq  rac{ n\mathrm{poly}( L, \exp(dB), 1/\delta) }{ \lambda \sqrt{m}}. \end{align*} Then, similar to the previous proof, we show:  egin{align*} \lambda_{\min}(H_{(
u)}(t) \otimes I_d ) \ge \omega\lambda / 2 -  rac{ n \mathrm{poly}( L, \exp(dB), 1/\delta) }{\lambda m^{1/2}}, \end{align*} and then:  egin{align} {\mathbb{E}}[ rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} t}] \leq - \varepsilon^2 C_1(1 -  rac{C_2n}{ m^{1/2}} ) \cdot {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D}) \end{align} where $C_1 = \omega \lambda / 2$ and $C_2 =\mathrm{poly}( L, \exp(dB), 1/\delta, 1/\lambda)$.

nodes.statement_short: Bound the kernel drift by the weight radius $R$ (three terms, anti-concentration for sign flips), apply eigenvalue perturbation, solve the loss ODE, then show the flow stays within $R$. The key step bounds activation-pattern flips via Gaussian anti-concentration and Markov.

nodes.name: Proof of Part 1
nodes.statement:
{\bf Proof of Part 1. }
    The proof proceeds in three steps.
nodes.statement_short: Three-step plan
nodes.section: H.1 A Sufficient Condition for Assumption~5.1

nodes.name: (i)
nodes.statement: (i) We bound the kernel perturbation $\|H_{(\nu)}'(t) - H_{(\nu)}'(0)\|_F$ in terms of the weight-perturbation radius $R$, treating $R$ as an a priori bound (Step~A).
nodes.statement_short: Bound kernel perturbation in terms of $R$
nodes.section: H.1 A Sufficient Condition for Assumption~5.1

nodes.name: (ii)
nodes.statement: (ii) We apply Fact~\ref{fac:lambda_min_perturb} to obtain a lower bound on $\lambda_{\min}(H_{(\nu)}'(t))$, then translate this into a loss-decay rate via Lemma~\ref{lem:learning_dynamics}.
nodes.statement_short: Eigenvalue bound then loss-decay rate
nodes.section: H.1 A Sufficient Condition for Assumption~5.1

nodes.name: (iii)
nodes.statement: (iii) Finally, we bound the maximum value of $R$ that the gradient flow itself produces, closing the bootstrapping argument. We begin with Step~A.

nodes.name: Drift hypothesis
nodes.statement:
First, we assume the condition $\| w_{(
u), r}(t) - w_{(
u), r}(0) \|_2 \leq R$ and $\| U_{(
u)}(t) - U_{(
u)}(0) \|_F \leq R$ as in Lemma~ef{lem:helpful_bounds}, which will be confirmed as a provable property below.

nodes.name: Three-term split
nodes.statement:
For any $p, q \in [nL]$, we have:
     egin{align*}
        & ~ | H_{(
u), p, q}'(t) - H_{(
u), p, q}'(0) | \
        = & ~  rac{1}{m}|  o_{(
u), p}(t)^	op o_{(
u), p}(t) \sum_{r\in [m]} \mathbb{I}\{ o_{(
u), p}(t)^	op w_{(
u), r}(t) > 0,  o_{(
u), q}(t)^	op w_{(
u), r}(t) > 0\} \
        & ~ -  o_{(
u), p}(0)^	op o_{(
u), p}(0) \sum_{r\in [m]} \mathbb{I}\{ o_{(
u), p}(0)^	op w_{(
u), r}(0) > 0,  o_{(
u), q}(0)^	op w_{(
u), r}(0) > 0\} | \
        \leq & ~  rac{1}{m} (Q_{(
u), p, q, 1} + Q_{(
u), p, q, 2} + Q_{(
u), p, q, 3}),
    \end{align*}
    where the first step follows from the definition of $H_{(
u), p, q}'(t)$, and the second step follows from the triangle inequality and defining:
     egin{align*}
        Q_{(
u), p, q, 1} := & ~ |  o_{(
u), p}(t)^	op o_{(
u), p}(t) \sum_{r\in [m]} \mathbb{I}\{ o_{(
u), p}(t)^	op w_{(
u), r}(t) > 0,  o_{(
u), q}(t)^	op w_{(
u), r}(t) > 0\} \
        & ~ -  o_{(
u), p}(0)^	op o_{(
u), p}(t) \sum_{r\in [m]} \mathbb{I}\{ o_{(
u), p}(t)^	op w_{(
u), r}(t) > 0,  o_{(
u), q}(t)^	op w_{(
u), r}(t) > 0\} |, \
        Q_{(
u), p, q, 2} := & ~ |  o_{(
u), p}(0)^	op o_{(
u), p}(t) \sum_{r\in [m]} \mathbb{I}\{ o_{(
u), p}(t)^	op w_{(
u), r}(t) > 0,  o_{(
u), q}(t)^	op w_{(
u), r}(t) > 0\} \
        & ~ -  o_{(
u), p}(0)^	op o_{(
u), p}(0) \sum_{r\in [m]} \mathbb{I}\{ o_{(
u), p}(t)^	op w_{(
u), r}(t) > 0,  o_{(
u), q}(t)^	op w_{(
u), r}(t) > 0\} |, \
        Q_{(
u), p, q, 3} := & ~ |  o_{(
u), p}(0)^	op o_{(
u), p}(0) \sum_{r\in [m]} \mathbb{I}\{ o_{(
u), p}(t)^	op w_{(
u), r}(t) > 0,  o_{(
u), q}(t)^	op w_{(
u), r}(t) > 0\} \
        & ~ -  o_{(
u), p}(0)^	op o_{(
u), p}(0) \sum_{r\in [m]} \mathbb{I}\{ o_{(
u), p}(0)^	op w_{(
u), r}(0) > 0,  o_{(
u), q}(0)^	op w_{(
u), r}(0) > 0\} |.
    \end{align*}
    We assume a constant $R$ that satisfies $\| w_{(
u), r}(t) - w_{(
u), r}(0) \|_2 \leq R$ and $\| U_{(
u)}(t) - U_{(
u)}(0)\|_F \leq R$.
nodes.statement_short: Split the kernel entry difference into $Q_1,Q_2,Q_3$
nodes.section: H.1 A Sufficient Condition for Assumption~5.1

nodes.name: Bounding Q1
nodes.statement:
{ f Bounding $Q_{(
u), p, q, 1}$.} We have:
     egin{align*}
        Q_{(
u), p, q, 1} \leq & ~ \Big|\Big( o_{(
u), p}(t) -  o_{(
u), p}(0) \Big)^	op  o_{(
u), q}(t) \
        & ~ \cdot \sum_{r=1}^m \mathbb{I}\{\langle  o_{(
u), p}(t), w_{(
u), r}(t)angle > 0, \langle  o_{(
u), q}(t), w_{(
u), r}(t)angle > 0\} \Big| \
        \leq & ~ m \Big|\Big( o_{(
u), p}(t) -  o_{(
u), p}(0) \Big)^	op  o_{(
u), q}(t) \Big| \
        \leq & ~ m \| o_{(
u), p}(t) -  o_{(
u), p}(0) \|_2 \cdot \|  o_{(
u), q}(t) \| \
        \leq & ~ m \cdot O(\sqrt{L}R ),
    \end{align*}
    where the first step follows from the definition of $Q_{(
u), p, q, 1}$ and Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, the second step follows from $\mathbb{I}\{\langle  o_{(
u), p}(t), w_{(
u), r}(t)angle > 0, \langle  o_{(
u), q}(t), w_{(
u), r}(t)angle > 0\} \leq 1$, the third step follows from Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, the last step follows from Part 6 and Part 13 of Lemma~ef{lem:helpful_bounds} and $\|  o_{(
u), q}(t) \| \leq O(1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $Q_1$ via attention-output drift
nodes.section: H.1 A Sufficient Condition for Assumption~5.1

nodes.name: Bounding Q2
nodes.statement:
{ f Bounding $Q_{(
u), p, q, 2}$.} The structure of $Q_{(
u),p,q,2}$ mirrors $Q_{(
u),p,q,1}$ with the roles of the two factors swapped: $Q_{(
u),p,q,2}$ pairs the {\it perturbed} factor $o_{(
u),p}(0)^	op o_{(
u),p}(t) - o_{(
u),p}(0)^	op o_{(
u),p}(0) = o_{(
u),p}(0)^	op  ig(o_{(
u),p}(t) - o_{(
u),p}(0) ig)$ with the same indicator sum (over $r\in[m]$). By Cauchy--Schwarz and Parts~5 and~13 of Lemma~ef{lem:helpful_bounds}:
     egin{align*}
        Q_{(
u), p, q, 2} &\le  ig|o_{(
u),p}(0)^	op ig(o_{(
u),p}(t) - o_{(
u),p}(0) ig) ig|\cdot \sum_{r=1}^m \mathbb{I}\{\cdot,\cdot\} \
        &\le \|o_{(
u),p}(0)\|_2\cdot \|o_{(
u),p}(t)-o_{(
u),p}(0)\|_2\cdot m \
        &\le m\cdot O(1)\cdot O(\sqrt{L}R) = m\cdot O(\sqrt L R).
    \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $Q_2$ symmetrically
nodes.section: H.1 A Sufficient Condition for Assumption~5.1

nodes.name: Bounding Q3
nodes.statement:
{ f Bounding $Q_{(
u), p, q, 3}$.} We define the following event:
     egin{align*}
        {\sf E}_{(
u), p, r} := & ~ \{ \exists w \in \mathbb{R}^d: \| w - w_{(
u), r}(0) \|_2 \leq R,\
        & ~ \mathbb{I}\{\langle  o_{(
u), p}(0), w_{(
u), r}(0) angle >0\} 
e \mathbb{I}\{\langle  o_{(
u), p}(t), w_{(
u), r}(t) angle >0\} \}.
    \end{align*}

    It is easy to hold that, once:
     egin{align*}
        & ~ |\langle  o_{(
u), p}(0), w_{(
u), r}(0) angle| \ge  O(\sqrt{L}R ) \cdot O(\sqrt{d}B) + O(1) \cdot R \
        \iff & ~ |\langle  o_{(
u), p}(0), w_{(
u), r}(0) angle| \ge  O(\sqrt{Ld}BR),
    \end{align*}
    the event ${\sf E}_{(
u), p, r}$ is false, since we combining Part 1, Part 9 and Part 13 of Lemma~ef{lem:helpful_bounds}, $\|  o_{(
u), q}(t) \| \leq O(1)$ and some simple algebra.

    Following Fact~ef{fac:inner_product_gaussian}, we have:
     egin{align*}
        \langle  o_{(
u), p}(0), w_{(
u), r}(0) angle \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \|  o_{(
u), p}(0)\|_2^2).
    \end{align*}

    We lower-bound $\|o_{(
u),p}(0)\|_2^2$ as follows. By Part~8 of Lemma~ef{lem:helpful_bounds}, for every $\ell' \in [\ell]$ we have $\sigma_{(
u),p,\ell'}(0) \ge \exp(-O(dB))/L$, and by Part~5 of Lemma~ef{lem:helpful_bounds}, $\|\Lambda_{(
u-1),i,\ell'}(0)\|_2 = \Theta(1)$. Picking the index $\ell^\star := \arg\max_{\ell'\in[\ell]} \|\Lambda_{(
u-1),i,\ell'}(0)\|_2$ and projecting:
     egin{align*}
        \|  o_{(
u), p}(0)\|_2^2 \ge  rac{\langle o_{(
u),p}(0),\Lambda_{(
u-1),i,\ell^\star}(0)angle^2}{\|\Lambda_{(
u-1),i,\ell^\star}(0)\|_2^2} \ge \sigma_{(
u),p,\ell^\star}(0)^2\,\|\Lambda_{(
u-1),i,\ell^\star}(0)\|_2^2 - O(L^{-1}) \ge \exp(-O(dB)),
    \end{align*}
    where the last step combines the bounds on $\sigma$ and $\|\Lambda\|$ above and the fact that the $L^{-2}$-cross-term contribution is dominated by the diagonal at the chosen index. Here $i = \lfloor p/Lfloor$ and $\ell = p mod L$.
    
    Then, the anti-concentration of $\langle  o_{(
u), p}(0), w_{(
u), r}(0) angle$ shows that:
     egin{align*}
        \Pr[{\sf E}_{(
u), p, r}]
        \leq & ~ \Pr ig[\, |\langle o_{(
u), p}(0), w_{(
u), r}(0)angle| \leq O(\sqrt{Ld}BR) \, ig] \
        \leq & ~  rac{2 \cdot O(\sqrt{Ld}BR)}{\sqrt{2\pi} \cdot \|  o_{(
u), p}(0)\|_2}  \
        \leq & ~ O(\sqrt{Ld}BR) \cdot \exp(O(dB)) \
        \leq & ~ O(\sqrt{L}R) \cdot \exp(O(dB)),
    \end{align*}
    where the first step follows from the necessary condition for ${\sf E}_{(
u),p,r}$ derived above, the second step follows from Fact~ef{fac:anti_concen_gaussian} (anti-concentration of a one-dimensional Gaussian), the third step follows from $\| o_{(
u),p}(0)\|_2^2 \ge \exp(-O(dB))$, and the last step absorbs $\sqrt{d}B$ into $\exp(O(dB))$.

    We have:
     egin{align*}
        {\mathbb{E}}[Q_{(
u), p, q, 3}] = & ~ {\mathbb{E}}\Big[ \Big|   o_{(
u), p}(0)^	op   o_{(
u), q}(0) \Big| \
        & ~ \cdot \sum_{r=1}^m \Big| \mathbb{I}\{\langle  o_{(
u), p}(t), w_{(
u), r}(t)angle > 0, \langle  o_{(
u), q}(t), w_{(
u), r}(t)angle > 0\} \
        & ~ \quad \quad ~ ~  - \mathbb{I}\{\langle  o_{(
u), p}(0), w_{(
u), r}(0)angle > 0, \langle  o_{(
u), q}(0), w_{(
u), r}(0)angle > 0\} \Big|\Big] \
        \leq & ~ {\mathbb{E}}\Big[ O(1)\cdot \sum_{r=1}^m \Big| \mathbb{I}\{\langle  o_{(
u), p}(t), w_{(
u), r}(t)angle > 0, \langle  o_{(
u), q}(t), w_{(
u), r}(t)angle > 0\} \
        & ~  - \mathbb{I}\{\langle  o_{(
u), p}(0), w_{(
u), r}(0)angle > 0, \langle  o_{(
u), q}(0), w_{(
u), r}(0)angle > 0\} \Big|\Big] \
        \leq & ~ O(1)\cdot \sum_{r=1}^m {\mathbb{E}}\Big[\Big| \mathbb{I}\{\langle  o_{(
u), p}(t), w_{(
u), r}(t)angle > 0, \langle  o_{(
u), q}(t), w_{(
u), r}(t)angle > 0\} \
        & ~  - \mathbb{I}\{\langle  o_{(
u), p}(0), w_{(
u), r}(0)angle > 0, \langle  o_{(
u), q}(0), w_{(
u), r}(0)angle > 0\} \Big|\Big] \
        \leq & ~ O(1)\cdot \sum_{r=1}^m {\mathbb{E}}\Big[\mathbb{I}\{ {\sf E}_{(
u), p, r} \cup {\sf E}_{(
u), q, r} \}\Big] \
        \leq & ~ O(1)\cdot \sum_{r=1}^m  \exp(O(dB)) \cdot \sqrt{L}R \
        \leq & ~ m O(\sqrt{L}R) \cdot \exp(O(dB)),
    \end{align*}
    where the first step follows from the definition of $Q_{(
u),p, q,3}$, the second step follows from $\| o_{(
u), p}(0)\|_2\leq O(1)$, the third and fourth step follow from the rules of expectation, the last two steps follow from $\Pr[{\sf E}_{(
u), p, r}] \leq O(\sqrt{L}R) \cdot \exp(O(dB))$ and simple algebra.

    Hence, using Markov's inequality (Lemma~ef{lem:markov}) with the failure budget $\delta'=\delta/(nL)^2$ to allow for a union bound over $(p,q)\in[nL]^2$ later, with a probability at least $1 - \delta'$, we have:
     egin{align*}
        Q_{(
u), p, q, 3} \leq m \cdot O(\sqrt{L}R) \cdot \exp(O(dB)) /\delta',
    \end{align*}
    so $Q_{(
u),p,q,3} \le m\cdot O(\sqrt L R)\cdot \exp(O(dB))\cdot (nL)^2/\delta$. The factor $(nL)^2/\delta$ enters $B = O(\sqrt{\log(Nmd(nL)^2/\delta)})$ as an additional $\log(nL)$ term, which is absorbed into the $\mathrm{poly}(L,d,B)$ constants of the final bound. The union-bound accounting makes the dependence explicit but does not change the polynomial / exponential structure.

nodes.name: Loss decay
nodes.statement:
Combining Lemma~ef{lem:learning_dynamics} (which gives $\dot{\mathcal{L}} = -\sum_
u g_
u^	op (H_
u\otimes I_d) g_
u$ with $g_
u := \mathrm{vec}(\mathrm{d}\mathcal{L}/\mathrm{d}\mu_{(
u)})$), the eigenvalue lower bound $\lambda_{\min}(H_{(
u)}(t)\otimes I_d) \ge \omega\lambda/2$ above, and the {\it corrected} Part~15 of Lemma~ef{lem:helpful_bounds} (which gives $\|g_
u\|^2 \asymp \varepsilon^2 \mathcal{L}/n$):
     egin{align*}
        {\mathbb{E}}\!\left[ rac{\mathrm{d} }{\mathrm{d} t}{\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})ight] \leq -  rac{\omega\lambda}{2}\sum_{
u\in[N]}\|g_
u\|^2 \le -  rac{C \cdot \omega \lambda N \cdot \varepsilon^2}{n} \cdot {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D}).
    \end{align*}

    Solving this ODE, we have:
     egin{align} {\mathbb{E}}[{\cal L}(T, \mathbb{D})] \leq \exp\!\left(-  rac{C \cdot \varepsilon^2  \omega\lambda NT}{n}ight) \cdot {\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D}).
    \end{align}

nodes.name: Bounding Gradient Norm
nodes.statement:
{\bf Bounding Gradient Norm.}
    Following Part 3 of Lemma~\ref{lem:helpful_bounds}, we have:
    \begin{align} & ~ \max_{T \ge 0} \max_{\nu\in [N]} \max_{r \in [m]} \| w_{(\nu), r}(T) -  w_{(\nu), r}(0) \|_2 \notag \\
        \leq & ~  \max_{T \ge 0} \int_{0}^T \max_{\nu\in [N]}\max_{r \in [m]}\| \frac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(s, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} w_{(\nu), r}(s)} \|_2 \mathrm{d} s \notag\\
        \leq & ~ \max_{T \ge 0} \int_{0}^T \exp(- C \cdot \varepsilon^2 \omega \lambda Ns) \cdot \varepsilon^2 {\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D}) \cdot \frac{\omega}{\sqrt{m}} \cdot O(\sqrt{d}B)  \mathrm{d} s \notag\\
        \leq & ~ \max_{T \ge 0} \int_{0}^T \exp(- C \cdot \varepsilon^2 \omega\lambda Ns) \cdot \frac{\varepsilon^2}{\sqrt{m}}  \mathrm{d} s \notag\\
        = & ~ \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} \max_{T \ge 0} - \frac{1}{C \omega \lambda N} \exp(- C \cdot \varepsilon^2 \omega \lambda Ns) \Big|_{s=0}^{s=T}  \notag\\
        \leq & ~ O(\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}  \omega\lambda N}) =: R
    \end{align}
    where the first step follows from Equation~\eqref{eq:ODE_update} and Cauchy-Schwartz inequality, the second step follows from Equation~\eqref{eq:dynamic_loss} and Part 15 of Lemma~\ref{lem:helpful_bounds}, the third step follows from Part 14 of Lemma~\ref{lem:helpful_bounds} and the choice of $\omega$, the last two steps follow from simple algebras and choosing
    \begin{align*}
        m = \Omega(\frac{n^2L^3\exp(O(dB))}{\omega^4\lambda^4\delta^2 N^2})
        \iff & ~ m/{\rm polylog}(N, m) = \Omega(\frac{n^2L^3\exp(Cd)}{\omega^4\lambda^4\delta^2 N^2}) \\
        \iff & ~ m/{\rm polylog}(m) = \Omega(\frac{n^2L^3\exp(Cd)}{\omega^4\lambda^4\delta^2 N^{\frac{4}{3}}}) \\
        \iff & ~ m^{\frac{2}{3}} = \Omega(\frac{n^2L^3\exp(Cd)}{\omega^4\lambda^4\delta^2 N^{\frac{4}{3}}}) \\
        \iff & ~ m = \Omega(\frac{n^3L^5\exp(Cd)}{\omega^6\lambda^6\delta^3 N^{2}})
    \end{align*}
    where these steps follow from simple algebras.

    Similarly, we have:
    \begin{align*}
        \max_{T \ge 0} \max_{\nu\in [N]}  \| U_{(\nu)}(T) -  U_{(\nu)}(0) \|_F \leq O(\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}  \omega\lambda N}) =: R
    \end{align*}

Assume the strengthened width condition $m = \Omega ig( rac{n^4 L^6 d^2 \exp(Cd)}{\omega^6 \lambda^8 \delta^4 N^4} ig)$. Then with probability at least $1-\delta$:  egin{enumerate} \item[ f (i)] $\max_{

nodes.name: Stop-time closure of the bootstrapping cycle
nodes.statement: The bounds in Lemma~\ref{lem:perturbations} (kernel stability), Lemma~\ref{lem:ffn_drift} (FFN drift), and Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence} (exponential loss decay) are proved {\it conditional} on each other through the per-step inequalities in Lemma~\ref{lem:helpful_bounds} (Parts~5,~9--13): kernel stability assumes the parameters stay inside the lazy ball; the lazy-ball drift bound $R=O(1/(\sqrt m\,\omega\lambda N))$ assumes exponential loss decay; and exponential loss decay assumes kernel stability. To break this circularity without resorting to a literal substitution chain, we use the standard stopping-time argument of \citep[Section 3]{dzps19}. Define the stopping time $\tau := \inf\{t \ge 0 : \|\theta(t)-\theta(0)\|_F > R\}$ with $R$ as above, and let $E_t = \{\tau > t\}$ be the event that the trajectory has not exited the lazy ball by time $t$. On $E_t$ all conclusions of Lemma~\ref{lem:perturbations} and Lemma~\ref{lem:ffn_drift} hold by construction; conditional on these, Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence} gives ${\cal L}(s, \mathbb{D}) \le \exp(-\alpha\varepsilon^2 s){\cal L}(0,\mathbb{D})$ for all $s\le t$. Integrating the gradient-flow drift on $[0,t]$ with this exponentially decaying loss recovers $\|\theta(t)-\theta(0)\|_F \le R/2$, contradicting $\tau \le t$. Hence $\tau = \infty$ almost surely, the lazy ball is never exited, and the three results hold {\it unconditionally} for all $t\ge 0$. This is the precise sense in which the bootstrapping cycle in Figure~\ref{fig:proof_dependency} closes.

nodes.statement_short: A stopping time on leaving the lazy ball shows the ball is never exited, closing the mutual dependence of kernel stability, FFN drift and convergence.

nodes.name: Training convergence
nodes.statement: Assuming Assumption~\ref{ass:positive_definite}, Definition~\ref{def:factors} and Definition~\ref{def:gd} hold, denote the failure probability $\delta \in (0, 0.1)$, then with a probability at least $ 1 - \delta$, we have: \begin{itemize} \item {\bf ($n, |\mathbb{B}|$)-Fixed Convergence.} Let $\alpha := C\cdot \omega\lambda N$ where $C>0$ is an absolute constant and $\omega N = \Theta(1/(L^2 d^{2.5}B^3))$ is a function of architecture only (Definition~\ref{def:gd}). Then: \begin{align*} {\cal L}({\sf T}, \mathbb{D}) \leq \exp\!\left(- \alpha \cdot \frac{\varepsilon^2 T}{\mathsf{N}}\right) \cdot {\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D}). \end{align*} Equivalently, writing $\bar\alpha := C\cdot\lambda$ (treating $L,d,B$ as fixed architectural constants and absorbing the polynomial $\omega N = \mathrm{poly}(1/L,1/d,1/B)$ into $\bar\alpha = \mathrm{poly}(L,d,B,\lambda)$), we have ${\cal L}({\sf T}, \mathbb{D}) \leq \exp(-\bar\alpha\,\varepsilon^2 T/\mathsf{N})\cdot {\cal L}(0,\mathbb{D})$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: With probability $1-\delta$, the training loss decays as $\exp(-\alpha\varepsilon^2T/{\sf N})$ with $\alpha=C\omega\lambda N$.
assumptions: Assuming Assumption~\ref{ass:positive_definite}, Definition~\ref{def:factors} and Definition~\ref{def:gd} hold
nodes.label: thm:convergence

nodes.name: Why the exponent has 1/N
nodes.statement: The factor $1/\mathsf{N} = 1/n$ in the exponent is essential: it traces directly to the average-loss convention $\mathcal{L} = \frac{1}{n}\|\mathsf{F}-\mathsf{Y}\|_F^2$ via Part~15 of Lemma~\ref{lem:helpful_bounds}. We track this $1/\mathsf{N}$ explicitly throughout, because $\mathsf{N}$ is one of the very scaling-law variables being analyzed and cannot be folded into a non-data ``constant''. Hiding this factor inside an absorbing constant ``$\alpha=\Theta(\lambda)$'' would produce a phase boundary of $\mathsf{C}\asymp\mathsf{N}^6$ rather than the correct $\mathsf{C}\asymp\mathsf{N}^7$; the qualitative two-stage shape is preserved either way, but the polynomial scaling differs by one power of $\mathsf{N}$.
nodes.statement_short: The $1/{\sf N}$ in the rate comes from the average-loss normalization; absorbing it would give a wrong ${\sf N}^6$ phase boundary.
nodes.label: rem:n_in_rate

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem I.2
nodes.statement: {\bf Proof of ($n, |\mathbb{B}|$)-Fixed Convergence.} We bound the per-step contribution of stochastic minibatching to the loss derivative, then combine with Lemma~\ref{lem:perturbations} to obtain an exponential decay. From Lemma~\ref{lem:perturbations} we have (with probability at least $1-\delta$), with the $1/n$ factor from Part~15: \begin{align} {\mathbb{E}}\Big[\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} t}{\cal L}(t,\mathbb{D})\Big] \le -\frac{C\cdot\omega\lambda N\cdot \varepsilon^2}{n}\cdot {\cal L}(t,\mathbb{D}). \end{align} The instantaneous fluctuation due to stochastic batching $\mathbb{B}(t)$ is controlled as follows. For any single per-sample gradient term, Lemma~\ref{lem:helpful_bounds} (Part 15) and the perturbation control of the kernel give: \begin{align*} \Big| \frac{\mathrm{d} }{\mathrm{d} t} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D}) \Big| \leq O\Big(\varepsilon^2\frac{N}{\sqrt{m}}\Big) \cdot {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D}), \end{align*} which arises from the bound $\|\frac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}}{\mathrm{d} \mu_{(\nu)}(t)}\|^2_F\asymp \varepsilon^2 {\cal L}(t,\mathbb{D})$ summed over $N$ layers, multiplied by the kernel norm $\|H_{(\nu)}(t)\|\le O(1/\sqrt{m})$ uniformly under Definition~\ref{def:gd}. Choosing $m = \Omega(n/(N\omega\lambda)^2)$ as in Definition~\ref{def:gd}, we get: \begin{align*} \Big| \frac{\mathrm{d} }{\mathrm{d} t} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D}) \Big| \leq o\Big(\varepsilon^2 \frac{\sqrt{|\mathbb{B}|}}{\sqrt{n}B} \omega \lambda \Big) \cdot {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D}), \end{align*} where $|\mathbb{B}| := \min_{t\ge 0} |\mathbb{B}(t)| \ge 1$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:hoeffding} (Hoeffding's inequality applied to the empirical mean over a batch of size $|\mathbb{B}|$), with probability at least $1-\delta$: \begin{align*} & ~ \Big| \frac{\mathrm{d} }{\mathrm{d} t} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D}) - {\mathbb{E}}\big[\frac{\mathrm{d} }{\mathrm{d} t} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D})\big] \Big| \\ \leq & ~ o\Big(\varepsilon^2\frac{\sqrt{|\mathbb{B}|}}{\sqrt{n}B} \omega \lambda \Big) \cdot \sqrt{\frac{n}{|\mathbb{B}|} \log(1/\delta)}\cdot {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D}) \\ \leq & ~ \frac{1}{2}C_1\cdot \varepsilon^2\cdot {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D}), \end{align*} where $C_1 := C\cdot \omega\lambda N/n$, the first step uses the per-sample bound and the variance reduction from a batch of size $|\mathbb{B}|$, and the second step uses $B = O(\sqrt{\log(Nmd/\delta)})$ together with Definition~\ref{def:gd} so that the stochastic deviation is at most half of the deterministic decay. Combining with Equation~\eqref{eq:exp_decay_full}: \begin{align*} \frac{\mathrm{d} }{\mathrm{d} t} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D}) \leq -\frac{1}{2}C_1\cdot \varepsilon^2 \cdot {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D}). \end{align*} Solving this scalar ODE inequality (Grönwall) yields: \begin{align*} {\cal L}(t, \mathbb{D}) \leq \exp\!\left(- \frac{C\cdot \varepsilon^2 \omega\lambda Nt}{n}\right) \cdot {\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D}). \end{align*} Setting $\alpha := C\cdot \omega\lambda N$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence}'s statement (we explicitly do {\it not} absorb the $1/n = 1/\mathsf{N}$ factor into the constant, because $\mathsf{N}$ is a scaling-law variable; see Remark~\ref{rem:n_in_rate}). With $t = {\sf T}$: \begin{align*} {\cal L}({\sf T}, \mathbb{D}) \leq \exp\!\left(- \frac{\alpha \cdot \varepsilon^2 T}{\mathsf{N}}\right) \cdot {\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D}), \end{align*} as claimed. Equivalently, absorbing the $\omega N = \mathrm{poly}(1/L,1/d,1/B)$ into a polynomial-in-$(L,d,B)$ constant $\bar\alpha := C\lambda$ gives the announced informal form.
nodes.statement_short: Kernel-stability decay plus a Hoeffding bound on minibatch fluctuations, then Gronwall.

nodes.name: Approximation bound using kernel regression
nodes.statement: Assuming we have arbitrary dataset size ${\sf N} \in (0, +\infty)$. Let all scaling law factors be defined as Definition~\ref{def:factors} and Assumption~\ref{ass:positive_definite} and Definition~\ref{def:gd} hold. Denote the failure probability $\delta \in (0, 0.1)$. For the Good Model Class $ {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})$ with training dataset $\mathbb{D}$ and target function $F^*: {\cal X} \to {\cal Y}$, we choose $\varepsilon \lesssim {\sf M}^{-1}$, with a probability at least $1 - \delta$, we have: \begin{align*} & ~ \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} {\mathbb{E}}_{(X, Y) \sim \mathcal{D}}[ \| F(X) - F^*(X)\|_F^2 ] \le {\sf M}^{-2}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: With $\varepsilon\lesssim{\sf M}^{-1}$, some trained transformer approximates $F^*$ to squared error ${\sf M}^{-2}$.
assumptions: Assuming we have arbitrary dataset size ${\sf N} \in (0, +\infty)$.
we choose $\varepsilon \lesssim {\sf M}^{-1}$
