nodes.name: Proof of Corollary I.4
nodes.statement:
The strategy is: (a) construct an idealized infinite-width NTK predictor $F^{m ntk}$, which is the kernel-regression solution against the target $F^*$, where the kernel is the {\it transformer-specific} layer-aggregated NTK $K(x,y):=\sum_{
u\in[N]}H_{(
u),x,y}(0)$ (Section~ef{sub:learning_dynamics}), {\it not} the 2-layer ReLU NTK on prefix-mean-pooled inputs; (b) by the realizability assumption that $F^*$ lies in the RKHS $\mathcal{H}_K$ of the layer-aggregated transformer NTK, $F^{m ntk} = F^*$ exactly within this RKHS; (c) apply the finite-width NTK approximation result of Theorem 3.2 in \citep{adh+19}, lifted to multi-layer transformers via the matrix-to-vector reduction of Appendix~ef{app_sub:matrix_to_vector}, to bound $|F(X,	heta(\infty)) - F^{m ntk}(X)|^2 \leq \varepsilon_{m app}^2$ where $\varepsilon_{m app}>0$ is the {\it approximation target accuracy} (a different parameter from the model scaling coefficient $\varepsilon$; see Remark~ef{rem:eps_double} below). Remark on the choice of kernel: a simpler 2-layer-MLP-on-prefix-mean kernel predictor of the form $F_\ell^{m ntk,simp}(X) = {\mathbb{E}}_w[{m ReLU}(\langle rac{1}{\ell}\sum_{\ell'\le\ell}X_{\ell'}, w(T)angle)] + X_\ell$ suffices for the {\it approximation upper bound} of Theorem~ef{cor:approximation:informal} when $F^*$ is itself realizable in the prefix-MLP RKHS; we record this simpler form below. For the general case where $F^*$ is realizable in the layer-aggregated transformer NTK $\mathcal{H}_K$ (which is a strictly larger RKHS), we use the transformer-NTK predictor $F^{m ntk}$ defined above. The bound $\inf\|F-F^*\|^2 \le {\sf M}^{-2}$ holds in both settings; the transformer-NTK formulation is the more general realizability assumption. { f Step (a): Construct the kernel predictor.} We construct the infinite-width transformer NTK predictor as the kernel-regression solution under the layer-aggregated kernel $K(x,y) = \sum_{
u\in[N]}H_{(
u),x,y}(0)$ defined in Section~ef{sub:learning_dynamics}:  egin{align*} F^{m ntk}(X) := \varepsilon \cdot K(\{X\},\mathbb{D}_*)\,K(\mathbb{D}_*,\mathbb{D}_*)^{-1}\,\widehat F^*(\mathbb{D}_*) + X, \end{align*} where $\mathbb{D}_*$ ranges over a dense countable subset of ${\cal X}$, $K$ is evaluated on the layer-by-layer kernel features $\{ eta_{(
u),p}(0), \gamma_{(
u),p}(0)\}$ from Lemma~ef{lem:learning_dynamics}, and $\widehat F^*$ is the centred target $F^*(X) - X_\ell$ (the residual-connection adjustment, since the model output already contains the residual $X_\ell$). The centred target is:  egin{align*} \widehat F^*_\ell({\cal A}) :=  egin{bmatrix} F^*_\ell({\cal A}_{1})^	op - {\cal A}_{1, \ell}^	op \ F^*_\ell({\cal A}_{2})^	op - {\cal A}_{2, \ell}^	op \ \vdots \ F^*_\ell({\cal A}_{|{\cal A}|})^	op - {\cal A}_{|{\cal A}|, \ell}^	op \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^{|{\cal A}| 	imes d}. \end{align*} For comparison and concreteness, we record the {\it simplified prefix-MLP-only} version that suffices when $F^*$ is realizable in the simpler prefix-MLP RKHS:  egin{align*} F_{\ell}^{m ntk,simp}(X) := & ~ \lim_{T 	o +\infty} \varepsilon \cdot {\mathbb{E}}_{w(0) \sim {\cal N}(0, I_d)}\left[ {m ReLU} \left( \left\langle  rac{1}{\ell} \sum_{\ell'=1}^{\ell} X_{\ell'}, w(T) ightangle ight) ight] + X_{\ell} \in \mathbb{R}^d \ = & ~ \varepsilon \cdot \Big({\cal K}_{\ell}(\{ X\}, {\cal X}) {\cal K}_{\ell}({\cal X}, {\cal X})^{-1} \widehat{F}_\ell({\cal X}) \Big)^	op, \end{align*} where ${\cal K}_\ell(\cdot,\cdot)$ is the prefix-mean ReLU NTK kernel detailed below. This simplified form uses only the standard 2-layer ReLU NTK and is what the approximation argument of \citep{adh+19} directly bounds; in the general transformer case, the Gram matrix $K$ above includes the additional $\gamma$-features from softmax-attention (Lemma~ef{lem:learning_dynamics}, the $U_{(
u)}$-kernel piece) that distinguish transformer NTK from a prefix-MLP NTK. For reference, the simplified Gram matrix is:  egin{align*} & ~ {\cal K}_{\ell, i, j}({\cal A}, {\cal B}) \ := & ~ \left(  rac{1}{\ell} \sum_{\ell'=1}^{\ell} {\cal A}_{i, \ell'}ight)^	op \left(  rac{1}{\ell} \sum_{\ell'=1}^{\ell} {\cal B}_{j, \ell'} ight) \cdot {\mathbb{E}}_{w \sim {\cal N}(0, I_d)}\left[\mathbb{I} \left\{\langle  rac{1}{\ell} \sum_{\ell'=1}^{\ell} {\cal A}_{i, \ell'}, w angle > 0,\ \langle  rac{1}{\ell} \sum_{\ell'=1}^{\ell} {\cal B}_{j, \ell'}, w angle > 0 ight\} ight]. \end{align*} The centred target $\widehat F$ accounts for the residual connection: the model output already contains $X_\ell$, so only $F^*(X) - X_\ell$ needs to be approximated by the kernel features. { f Step (b): Reduce approximation to RKHS interpolation.} The approximation error is:  egin{align*} \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} {\mathbb{E}}_{(X, Y) \sim {\cal D}} ig[ \| F(X) - F^*(X)\|_F^2  ig] = & ~ \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} \| F - F^*\|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2 \ \leq & ~ \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} \| F - F^{m ntk}\|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2 + \| F^{m ntk} - F^*\|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2 \ = & ~ \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} \| F - F^{m ntk}\|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2, \end{align*} where the first step rewrites the expectation as an $L^F({\cal X})$ norm, the second step is a triangle decomposition, and the third step uses $F^{m ntk} = F^*$ {\it under the realizability assumption} that $F^*$ lies in the RKHS $\mathcal{H}_K$ of the layer-aggregated transformer NTK $K = \sum_
u H_{(
u)}(0)$. The realizability assumption is the analogue of the standard NTK-realizability assumption used in \citep{adh+19, dzps19}; it is automatically satisfied if $F^*$ is itself a transformer of the same architecture (with potentially different weights), and is broader than realizability in any single $ eta$- or $\gamma$-feature subspace. { f Step (c): Apply finite-width approximation.} By Theorem 3.2 in \citep{adh+19}, for any approximation target accuracy $\varepsilon_{m app} > 0$ (distinct from the model scaling $\varepsilon$; see Remark~ef{rem:eps_double}), taking $m = \Theta(\mathrm{poly}(1/\varepsilon_{m app}))$ yields, with probability at least $1-\delta$ over $	heta(0)$:  egin{align*} \lim_{{\sf T} ightarrow \infty}\left|F_{\ell, k}(X, 	heta({\sf T})) - F_{\ell, k}^{m ntk}(X) ight|^2 \leq \varepsilon_{m app}^2 \quad 	ext{for all } X\in {\cal X},\, \ell\in[L],\, k\in[d]. \end{align*} Summing over $\ell\in[L]$ and $k\in[d]$:  egin{align} \lim_{{\sf T} 	o \infty} {\mathbb{E}}_{X\sim {\cal D}} ig[ \| F(X, 	heta({\sf T})) - F^{m ntk}(X) \|_F^2  ig] \leq \varepsilon_{m app}^2. \end{align} Combining with Step (b) and choosing $\varepsilon_{m app} \lesssim {\sf M}^{-1}$ (so that the per-coordinate target accuracy of the bound from \citep{adh+19} matches the desired ${\sf M}^{-2}$ squared error after summing $Ld$ coordinates):  egin{align*} \lim_{{\sf T} 	o \infty} \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} {\mathbb{E}}_{(X, Y) \sim {\cal D}} ig[ \| F(X) - F^*(X)\|_F^2  ig] \leq \varepsilon_{m app}^2 \leq {\sf M}^{-2}, \end{align*} which is the claim. We emphasize that $\varepsilon_{m app}$ is a property of the function class, realized through the width $m$, and is decoupled from the model-scaling coefficient: the proof of Theorem~ef{thm:scaling_law}, which sets the model scaling to $\varepsilon = \xi/{\sf N}$, does not invoke the specialization $\varepsilon_{m app} \lesssim {\sf M}^{-1}$ of this corollary, but the $\varepsilon$-parametric form of the generalization bound (see Equation~\eqref{eq:dr_bound}).
nodes.statement_short: Build the infinite-width transformer-NTK predictor, use realizability to identify it with $F^*$, then apply the finite-width approximation of Arora et al.

nodes.name: Strategy
nodes.statement: The strategy is: (a) construct an idealized infinite-width NTK predictor $F^{\rm ntk}$, which is the kernel-regression solution against the target $F^*$, where the kernel is the {\it transformer-specific} layer-aggregated NTK $K(x,y):=\sum_{\nu\in[N]}H_{(\nu),x,y}(0)$ (Section~\ref{sub:learning_dynamics}), {\it not} the 2-layer ReLU NTK on prefix-mean-pooled inputs; (b) by the realizability assumption that $F^*$ lies in the RKHS $\mathcal{H}_K$ of the layer-aggregated transformer NTK, $F^{\rm ntk} = F^*$ exactly within this RKHS; (c) apply the finite-width NTK approximation result of Theorem 3.2 in \citep{adh+19}, lifted to multi-layer transformers via the matrix-to-vector reduction of Appendix~\ref{app_sub:matrix_to_vector}, to bound $|F(X,\theta(\infty)) - F^{\rm ntk}(X)|^2 \leq \varepsilon_{\rm app}^2$ where $\varepsilon_{\rm app}>0$ is the {\it approximation target accuracy} (a different parameter from the model scaling coefficient $\varepsilon$; see Remark~\ref{rem:eps_double} below).
nodes.statement_short: Three-step strategy

nodes.name: Choice of kernel
nodes.statement: Remark on the choice of kernel: a simpler 2-layer-MLP-on-prefix-mean kernel predictor of the form $F_\ell^{\rm ntk,simp}(X) = {\mathbb{E}}_w[{\rm ReLU}(\langle\frac{1}{\ell}\sum_{\ell'\le\ell}X_{\ell'}, w(T)\rangle)] + X_\ell$ suffices for the {\it approximation upper bound} of Theorem~\ref{cor:approximation:informal} when $F^*$ is itself realizable in the prefix-MLP RKHS; we record this simpler form below. For the general case where $F^*$ is realizable in the layer-aggregated transformer NTK $\mathcal{H}_K$ (which is a strictly larger RKHS), we use the transformer-NTK predictor $F^{\rm ntk}$ defined above. The bound $\inf\|F-F^*\|^2 \le {\sf M}^{-2}$ holds in both settings; the transformer-NTK formulation is the more general realizability assumption.
nodes.statement_short: Remark: simpler prefix-MLP kernel suffices in a special case

nodes.name: Step (a)
nodes.statement_short: Construct the kernel-regression predictor

nodes.name: Step (b)
nodes.statement:
{\bf Step (b): Reduce approximation to RKHS interpolation.} The approximation error is:
    \begin{align*}
        \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} {\mathbb{E}}_{(X, Y) \sim {\cal D}}\big[ \| F(X) - F^*(X)\|_F^2 \big]
        = & ~ \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})}  \| F - F^*\|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2 \\
        \leq & ~ \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})}  \| F - F^{\rm ntk}\|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2 + \| F^{\rm ntk} - F^*\|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2 \\
        = & ~ \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})}  \| F - F^{\rm ntk}\|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2,
    \end{align*}
    where the first step rewrites the expectation as an $L^F({\cal X})$ norm, the second step is a triangle decomposition, and the third step uses $F^{\rm ntk} = F^*$ {\it under the realizability assumption} that $F^*$ lies in the RKHS $\mathcal{H}_K$ of the layer-aggregated transformer NTK $K = \sum_\nu H_{(\nu)}(0)$. The realizability assumption is the analogue of the standard NTK-realizability assumption used in \citep{adh+19, dzps19}; it is automatically satisfied if $F^*$ is itself a transformer of the same architecture (with potentially different weights), and is broader than realizability in any single $\beta$- or $\gamma$-feature subspace.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to RKHS interpolation under realizability

nodes.name: Step (c)
nodes.statement_short: Apply finite-width NTK approximation and choose $\varepsilon_{\rm app}\lesssim{\sf M}^{-1}$

nodes.name: Finite-width approximation error
nodes.statement: \lim_{{\sf T} \to \infty} {\mathbb{E}}_{X\sim {\cal D}}\big[ \| F(X, \theta({\sf T})) - F^{\rm ntk}(X) \|_F^2 \big] \leq \varepsilon_{\rm app}^2.
nodes.label: eq:approx_vareps

nodes.name: Two distinct uses of epsilon
nodes.statement: The symbol $\varepsilon$ is used in two distinct senses in the kernel-NTK literature: (a) the {\it model scaling coefficient} $\varepsilon>0$ that multiplies the residual sum $\varepsilon\sum_\nu \mu_{(\nu)}$ in our model definition (Equation~\eqref{eq:F}), used throughout to control the lazy-regime norm; (b) the {\it approximation target accuracy} $\varepsilon_{\rm app}>0$ that appears in the finite-width NTK approximation bound $\|F-F^{\rm ntk}\|^2\le\varepsilon_{\rm app}^2$ of \citep{adh+19}. We disambiguate these by writing $\varepsilon$ for (a) and $\varepsilon_{\rm app}$ for (b). The choice $\varepsilon_{\rm app} \lesssim {\sf M}^{-1}$ in Step (c) is the standard balance: setting $m = \Theta(\mathrm{poly}(1/\varepsilon_{\rm app}))$ as in \citep{adh+19} produces a width that is consistent with our $m = \Omega(\mathsf{N}^3 \cdot \mathrm{poly})$ from Definition~\ref{def:gd}. The approximation bound $\inf\|F-F^*\|^2 \le {\sf M}^{-2}$ holds with target accuracy $\varepsilon_{\rm app} = {\sf M}^{-1}$ in the sense of \citep{adh+19}, which is what enters the generalization bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:generalization}.
nodes.statement_short: Separates the model scaling coefficient $\varepsilon$ from the approximation accuracy $\varepsilon_{\rm app}$.
nodes.label: rem:eps_double

nodes.name: ERM model class over the full parameter space
nodes.statement: Within the scope of this subsection, we redefine the model class as \begin{align*} {\cal F}_{\sf M, N}(\mathbb{D}) := \{F(\cdot, \theta) : \theta \in \mathbb{R}^{\sf M}\}. \end{align*} That is, ${\cal F}_{\sf M, N}(\mathbb{D})$ collects every realizable parameterization of the architecture (Equation~\eqref{eq:F}) of total parameter count $\sf M$, rather than the closure of training trajectories. Consequently, the infimum $\inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, N}(\mathbb{D})} \Delta {\cal R}(F)$ corresponds to the empirical risk minimizer (ERM) over the parameter space, and the generalization bound below applies to the ERM directly via the standard nonparametric statistics tool of Lemma~\ref{thm:gen}. The approximation error of the ERM in this class is independently bounded through the RKHS construction in Corollary~\ref{cor:approximation}; the bound is therefore not contingent on $\lim_{{\sf T} \to \infty}$ and addresses the technical concern that the optimization endpoint and the ERM need not coincide.
nodes.section: J.1 Generalization Bound of Empirical Risk Minimizer
nodes.statement_short: Within J.1 the model class is every parameterization with ${\sf M}$ parameters, so the infimum is the ERM.
nodes.label: rem:H1

nodes.name: Covering entropy
nodes.statement: For a metric space $({\cal S}, {\rm d})$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, a finite set ${\cal S}' \subset \overline{\cal S}$ is called $\varepsilon$-covering if for any $x \in {\cal S}$ there exists $y \in {\cal S}'$ such that ${\rm d}(x, y) \leq \varepsilon$, and the logarithm of the minimum cardinality of $\varepsilon$-covering is called covering $\varepsilon$-entropy and denoted by $V_{({\cal S}, {\rm d})}(\varepsilon)$. Here, $\overline{\cal S}$ is the completion of ${\cal S}$ with respect to the metric ${\rm d}$.
nodes.section: J.1 Generalization Bound of Empirical Risk Minimizer
nodes.origin_citation: van der Vaart & Wellner 1996; Yang & Barron 1999
nodes.genus: logarithm of the minimum cardinality of $\varepsilon$-covering

nodes.name: ERM generalization bound (Lemma 11 of Schmidt-Hieber)
nodes.statement: For any $\mathbb{D} \subset {\cal D}$, let $F$ be the empirical risk minimizer taking values in ${\cal F}_{\sf M, N}(\mathbb{D})$. Suppose every element $F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, N}$ satisfies ${\rm d}(F) := \max_{\ell \in [L]} \max_{k \in [d]} \| F_{\ell, k} \|_{L^{\infty}({\cal X})} \leq B_F$ for some fixed $B_F > 0$. Then, for an arbitrary $\varepsilon > 0$, if $V_{({\cal F}, {\rm d})}(\varepsilon) \ge 1$, then \begin{align*} \| F - F^* \|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2 \leq 4 \inf_{F' \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, N}(\mathbb{D})} \| F' - F^* \|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2 + Ld \cdot O\!\left( \frac{(B_F^2+\xi^2)V_{({\cal F}_{\sf M, N}(\mathbb{D}), {\rm d})}(\varepsilon)}{n} + (B_F+\xi)\varepsilon\right). \end{align*}
nodes.section: J.1 Generalization Bound of Empirical Risk Minimizer
nodes.statement_short: The ERM's squared error is at most four times the best approximation error plus covering-entropy and noise terms.
assumptions: Suppose every element $F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, N}$ satisfies ${\rm d}(F) := \max_{\ell \in [L]} \max_{k \in [d]}  \| F_{\ell, k} \|_{L^{\infty}({\cal X})} \leq B_F$ for some fixed $B_F > 0$
nodes.label: thm:gen

nodes.name: Source of the ERM lemma
nodes.statement: Lemma~\ref{thm:gen} is Lemma 11 in the third arXiv version of \citep{sch17}, and it was further modified by Theorem 2.1 in \citep{sat17} and Proposition 4 in \citep{suz18}. We make some minor adjustments to our settings.
nodes.section: J.1 Generalization Bound of Empirical Risk Minimizer

nodes.statement: $\delta \in (0, 0.1)$. nodes.name: Proof of Lemma J.5
nodes.statement: {\bf Proof of Part 1.} Following Part 5 of Lemma~\ref{lem:helpful_bounds} and Equation~\eqref{eq:F}, we have: \begin{align*} \max_{\ell \in [L], X \in {\cal X}}\| F_\ell(X) \|_2^2 \leq O(\varepsilon^2). \end{align*} We have: \begin{align*} \| F_{\ell} \|_{L^{\infty}({\cal X})} \leq & ~ \left(\max_{\ell \in [L]} \int_{\cal X} \| F_\ell(X) \|_\infty^2 \mathrm{d} X \right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \\ \leq & ~ \left( O(\varepsilon^2) \right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \\ \leq & ~ O(\varepsilon), \end{align*} where the first step follows from the $L^\infty$ norm, the second step follows from $\max_{\ell \in [L], X \in {\cal X}}\| F_\ell(X) \|_2^2 \leq O(\varepsilon^2)$, the last step follows from simple algebras. {\bf Proof of Part 2.} Here, we use $R$ to denote the weight distance between arbitrary two functions $F, F' \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, N}$, following Part 3 of Lemma~\ref{lem:helpful_bounds} and some simple algebras, $R$ is bounded by $O({\sf M}B\varepsilon)$ with $\max_{F, F' \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, N}} \|F - F'\|_{L^F({\cal X})} \leq \varepsilon$, and the space of ${\cal F}_{\sf M, N}$ is an $\sf M$-dimensional ball with radius $O({\sf M}B\varepsilon)$. Thus, for any step size $\zeta > 0$, the gap is bounded by: \begin{align*} \|F - F'\|_{L^F({\cal X})} \leq \varepsilon \sqrt{Ld} \zeta \leq O(\varepsilon^2), \end{align*} where the first step follows from the definition of $F$ and Part 13 of Lemma~\ref{lem:helpful_bounds}, the second step follows from choosing $\zeta = \varepsilon$. We need at most $O(1)^{\sf M}$ numbers to cover this set. Then we have the logarithm of the covering number: \begin{align*} V_{({\cal F}_{\sf M, N}, {\rm d})}(\zeta) \leq O(1) \end{align*}

Then, with a probability at least $1 - \delta$, there exists: \begin{align*} \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, N}(\mathbb{D})} \sup_{\mathbb{D} \in {\cal D}} \Delta{\cal R}(F) \leq \big(4{\sf M}^{-1} + Ld\cdot \xi\big) \cdot {\sf M}^{-1} + \frac{Ld \cdot\xi^2}{\sf N}. \end{align*} We retain the $Ld$ factors explicitly in both terms because $L$ (sequence length) and $d$ (embedding dimension) are scaling-law variables independent of the noise level $\xi$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem J.6
nodes.statement:
We first reduce the excess risk to a function-space discrepancy. By the definitions of ${\cal R}(\cdot)$ and $\Delta{\cal R}(\cdot)$ (Section~ef{sub:setups}) and the data model $Y = F^*(X) + \Xi$:  egin{align} \Delta{\cal R}(F) = & ~ {\cal R}(F) - {\cal R}(F^*) 
otag \ = & ~ {\mathbb{E}}_{(X, Y) \sim {\cal D}}\left[ \| F(X) - Y\|_F^2 - \| F^*(X) - Y\|_F^2 ight] 
otag \ = & ~ {\mathbb{E}}_{(X, Y) \sim {\cal D}}\left[ \| F(X) - F^*(X) - \Xi\|_F^2 - \| \Xi \|_F^2 ight] 
otag \ = & ~ {\mathbb{E}}_{(X, Y) \sim {\cal D}}\left[ \| F(X) - F^*(X) \|_F^2 - 2\langle \mathrm{vec}(F(X) - F^*(X)),\mathrm{vec}(\Xi)angle + \|\Xi\|_F^2 - \| \Xi \|_F^2 ight] 
otag \ = & ~ {\mathbb{E}}_{(X, Y) \sim {\cal D}}\left[ \| F(X) - F^*(X) \|_F^2 ight]
otag \ = & ~ \| F - F^* \|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2, \end{align} where the first step follows from the definitions of ${\cal R}$ and $\Delta {\cal R}$, the second step follows from $Y = F^*(X) + \Xi$, the third step follows from simple algebras, the fourth step follows from the independence of $X$ and $\Xi$, ${\mathbb{E}}[\Xi] = { f 0}_{L 	imes d}$ (and so ${\mathbb{E}}[\langle\mathrm{vec}(F(X) - F^*(X)),\mathrm{vec}(\Xi)angle]=0$), the fifth step follows from cancellation of the $\|\Xi\|_F^2$ terms, the sixth step follows from the definition of the $L^F({\cal X})$ norm. Next, we bound the approximation term. Combining Corollary~ef{cor:approximation} (with the choice $\varepsilon \lesssim {\sf M}^{-1}$) and the redefinition of ${\cal F}_{\sf M, N}(\mathbb{D})$ in Remark~ef{rem:H1}, we have:  egin{align} \inf_{F' \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, N}(\mathbb{D})} \| F' - F^* \|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2 \leq {\sf M}^{-2}. \end{align} { f Bounding the generalization (estimation) terms.} Lemma~ef{thm:gen} requires control of two quantities: the linear-in-$\varepsilon$ term $(B_F+\xi)\varepsilon$ and the covering-entropy term $(B_F^2+\xi^2) V_{({\cal F}_{\sf M, N}(\mathbb{D}),{m d})}(\varepsilon)/{\sf N}$. We bound them in turn.  egin{align} (B_F+\xi)\varepsilon \leq (\varepsilon + \xi)\varepsilon = \varepsilon^2 + \xi\varepsilon \leq O(\xi\varepsilon), \end{align} where the inequality uses $B_F \leq O(\varepsilon)$ from Part 1 of Lemma~ef{lem:generalization_helper} and the dominance $\varepsilon^2 \leq \xi\varepsilon$ for the regime $\varepsilon \leq \xi$ that follows from the choice $\varepsilon = \Theta(1/{\sf M})$ with $\xi$ being a fixed noise level. Similarly,  egin{align}  rac{(B_F^2+\xi^2)V_{({\cal F}_{\sf M, N}(\mathbb{D}), {m d})}(\varepsilon)}{\sf N} \leq O\left( rac{\varepsilon^2+\xi^2}{\sf N}ight) \leq O\left( rac{\xi^2}{\sf N}ight), \end{align} where the first step combines Part 1 ($B_F^2\leq O(\varepsilon^2)$) and Part 2 ($V \leq O(1)$) of Lemma~ef{lem:generalization_helper}, and the second step uses $\varepsilon^2 \leq \xi^2$ in the regime considered. { f Combining the bounds.} Plugging Equation~\eqref{eq:approx_term}, Equation~\eqref{eq:bf_xi_eps}, and Equation~\eqref{eq:cov_term} into Lemma~ef{thm:gen} yields:  egin{align*} \| F - F^* \|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2 \leq & ~ 4 \inf_{F' \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, N}(\mathbb{D})} \| F' - F^* \|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2 + Ld \cdot O\!\left( rac{\xi^2}{\sf N} + \xi\varepsilonight) \ \leq & ~ 4 {\sf M}^{-2} + Ld \cdot O\!\left( rac{\xi^2}{\sf N} +  rac{\xi}{\sf M}ight) \ \leq & ~  ig(4 {\sf M}^{-1} + Ld\cdot\xi ig) \cdot {\sf M}^{-1} +  rac{Ld\cdot \xi^2}{\sf N}, \end{align*} where the second step uses $\varepsilon = \Theta({\sf M}^{-1})$ and the third step regroups summands. We retain $L$ and $d$ explicitly in both terms because they are scaling-law variables independent of $\xi$ (sequence length and embedding dimension, not noise scale). Combining with Equation~\eqref{eq:bound_delta_R} and taking the infimum over $F\in {\cal F}_{\sf M, N}(\mathbb{D})$ and the supremum over the data distribution, we obtain:  egin{align*} \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, N}(\mathbb{D})} \sup_{\mathbb{D} \in {\cal D}} \Delta{\cal R}(F) \leq  ig(4{\sf M}^{-1} + Ld\cdot \xi ig) \cdot {\sf M}^{-1} +  rac{Ld \cdot\xi^2}{\sf N}. \end{align*} This completes the proof.

nodes.name: Excess risk identity
nodes.statement:
We first reduce the excess risk to a function-space discrepancy. By the definitions of ${\cal R}(\cdot)$ and $\Delta{\cal R}(\cdot)$ (Section~\ref{sub:setups}) and the data model $Y = F^*(X) + \Xi$:
    \begin{align} \Delta{\cal R}(F) = & ~ {\cal R}(F) - {\cal R}(F^*) \notag \\
        = & ~ {\mathbb{E}}_{(X, Y) \sim {\cal D}}\left[ \| F(X) - Y\|_F^2 - \| F^*(X) - Y\|_F^2 \right] \notag \\
        = & ~ {\mathbb{E}}_{(X, Y) \sim {\cal D}}\left[ \| F(X) - F^*(X) - \Xi\|_F^2 - \| \Xi \|_F^2 \right] \notag \\
        = & ~ {\mathbb{E}}_{(X, Y) \sim {\cal D}}\left[ \| F(X) - F^*(X) \|_F^2 - 2\langle \mathrm{vec}(F(X) - F^*(X)),\mathrm{vec}(\Xi)\rangle + \|\Xi\|_F^2 - \| \Xi \|_F^2 \right] \notag \\
        = & ~ {\mathbb{E}}_{(X, Y) \sim {\cal D}}\left[ \| F(X) - F^*(X) \|_F^2  \right]\notag  \\
        = & ~  \| F - F^* \|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2,
    \end{align}
    where the first step follows from the definitions of ${\cal R}$ and $\Delta {\cal R}$, the second step follows from $Y = F^*(X) + \Xi$, the third step follows from simple algebras, the fourth step follows from the independence of $X$ and $\Xi$, ${\mathbb{E}}[\Xi] = {\bf 0}_{L \times d}$ (and so ${\mathbb{E}}[\langle\mathrm{vec}(F(X) - F^*(X)),\mathrm{vec}(\Xi)\rangle]=0$), the fifth step follows from cancellation of the $\|\Xi\|_F^2$ terms, the sixth step follows from the definition of the $L^F({\cal X})$ norm.

nodes.name: Two-stage scaling law with matching bounds
nodes.statement: Let all pre-conditions hold as Corollary~\ref{cor:approximation} and choose $\varepsilon = \Theta(\xi/{\sf N})$. Then, with a probability at least $1 - \delta$, the following condition divides the scaling trend into two stages: \begin{align} {\sf C} > \frac{{\sf N}^7\log( {\sf N} \cdot Ld/\xi^2)}{\xi^2}. \end{align} \begin{itemize} \item {\it Stage I (Compute-Starved Stage).} If Equation~\eqref{eq:cond_C:formal} does not hold, then there exist constants $\alpha,C,c_2',C_{\rm opt}'>0$ depending polynomially on $(L,d,1/\lambda,1/\omega)$ such that: \begin{align*} c_2'\,\exp\!\big(-C_{\rm opt}'\, \kappa_{\sf opt}\cdot \xi^2{\sf C}/{\sf N}^7\big)\cdot{\cal L}(0,\mathbb{D}) \;\le\; \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} \sup_{\mathbb{D} \in {\cal D}} \Delta{\cal R}(F) \;\le\; C \exp\!\big(-\alpha\, \xi^2{\sf C}/{\sf N}^7\big) \cdot {\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D}), \end{align*} where $\kappa_{\sf opt}\in[\sqrt{\lambda/\lambda_{\max}},\,1]$ is a square-root-condition-number factor that distinguishes the upper from the lower bound (see Theorem~\ref{thm:lower_opt} and Remark~\ref{rem:tightness}). \item {\it Stage II (Data-Limited Stage).} If Equation~\eqref{eq:cond_C:formal} holds, then there exists $c_1'>0$ such that: \begin{align*} c_1'\cdot \xi^{12/7}\cdot \widetilde\Omega\!\big({\sf C}^{-1/7}\big) \;\le\; \inf_{F\in{\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} \sup_{\mathbb{D} \in {\cal D}} \Delta{\cal R}(F) \;\le\; \xi^{12/7} \cdot O\!\Big( \frac{{\sf C}}{W({\sf C}/\xi^{12})} \Big)^{-1/7} \le \xi^{12/7} \cdot \widetilde{O}\!\big({\sf C}^{-1/7}\big), \end{align*} where $W(\cdot)$ is the Lambert $W$ function and $\widetilde O,\widetilde \Omega$ hide $\log {\sf C}$ factors. \end{itemize} The upper bounds follow from the analysis below; the lower bounds follow from Corollary~\ref{cor:lower_data_limited} (statistical) and Theorem~\ref{thm:lower_opt} (optimization-side). The boundary $\mathsf{N}^7$ and Stage~II rate $\xi^{12/7}\mathsf{C}^{-1/7}$ both arise from the $1/\mathsf{N}$ factor in the convergence rate (Remark~\ref{rem:n_in_rate}) that the average-loss normalization contributes; the Pythia compute-frontier exponent $\eta=0.120$ in Appendix~\ref{app_sub:wikitext_results} is in the same range as the theoretical $1/7\approx 0.143$.
nodes.statement_short: Below ${\sf C}\approx{\sf N}^7\log/\xi^2$ the excess risk is $\exp(-\Theta(\xi^2{\sf C}/{\sf N}^7))$; above it, $\xi^{12/7}\widetilde\Theta({\sf C}^{-1/7})$, with matching lower bounds.
assumptions: Let all pre-conditions hold as Corollary~\ref{cor:approximation} and choose $\varepsilon = \Theta(\xi/{\sf N})$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem J.7
nodes.statement:
Let $F = F(\cdot, 	heta({\sf T}))$ denote the optimizing function obtained from running gradient flow until time $\sf T$, i.e. $F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})$ in the sense of Definition~ef{def:gd}. Let $F' \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, N}(\mathbb{D})$ be the empirical risk minimizer over the (re-defined; see Remark~ef{rem:H1}) parameter space. By the triangle inequality in $L^F({\cal X})$ norm:  egin{align*} \Delta {\cal R}(F) \leq & ~ \| F - F^*\|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2 \ \leq & ~ \left(\| F - F'\|_{L^F({\cal X})} + \| F' - F^*\|_{L^F({\cal X})}ight)^2, \end{align*} where the first step follows from Equation~\eqref{eq:bound_delta_R}, the second step follows from the triangle inequality. We control the {\it optimization} term $\|F-F'\|_{L^F({\cal X})}$ via the kernel-stable gradient flow, carrying the $1/\mathsf{N}$ factor of Theorem~ef{thm:convergence} (Remark~ef{rem:n_in_rate}) through the integration. Bounding the residual weight movement after time $\sf T$:  egin{align*} & ~ \max_{
u\in [N]} \max_{r \in [m]} \| w_{(
u), r}({\sf T}) - w_{(
u), r}(+\infty) \|_2 
otag \ \leq & ~ \int_{\sf T}^\infty \max_{
u\in [N]}\max_{r \in [m]}\Big\|  rac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(s, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} w_{(
u), r}(s)} \Big\|_2 \mathrm{d} s 
otag\ \leq & ~ \int_{\sf T}^\infty \varepsilon \cdot \sqrt{{\cal L}(s, \mathbb{D}) }\mathrm{d} s 
otag\ \leq & ~ \varepsilon \int_{\sf T}^\infty \exp\Big(- rac{\alpha \varepsilon^2 s}{2\mathsf{N}}\Big) \cdot \sqrt{ {\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D})}\mathrm{d} s \ = & ~  rac{2\mathsf{N}}{\alpha \varepsilon} \exp\Big(- rac{\alpha \varepsilon^2 \mathsf{T}}{2\mathsf{N}}\Big) \cdot \sqrt{{\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D})}, \end{align*} where the first step follows from the gradient-flow update Equation~\eqref{eq:ODE_update} and Cauchy--Schwarz, the second step from Part~15 of Lemma~ef{lem:helpful_bounds}, the third step from Theorem~ef{thm:convergence} after taking square roots, and the last step is direct integration. Following Part 12 of Lemma~ef{lem:helpful_bounds} (which transforms parameter-space distance into the $L^F({\cal X})$ functional distance) and the definition of $F$, we get:  egin{align*} \| F - F'\|_{L^F({\cal X})} \leq & ~ \min\Big\{ P\exp\Big(- rac{\alpha \varepsilon^2 \mathsf{T}}{2\mathsf{N}}\Big),\, O(1) \Big\} \cdot \sqrt{{\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D})} \leq \exp\Big(- rac{\alpha \varepsilon^2 \mathsf{T}}{4\mathsf{N}}\Big) \cdot \sqrt{{\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D})}, \qquad P :=  rac{2CL\mathsf{N}}{\alpha\varepsilon}, \end{align*} with the following bookkeeping. The $O(1)\cdot\sqrt{{\cal L}(0,\mathbb{D})}$ branch of the minimum is the crude bound: every $F$ in the Good Model Class keeps its hidden states and outputs at the initialization scale (Parts~3 and~5 of Lemma~ef{lem:helpful_bounds}), so $\|F-F'\|_{L^F({\cal X})} = O(\sqrt{Ld}) = O(\sqrt{{\cal L}(0,\mathbb{D})})$, the latter since ${\cal L}(0,\mathbb{D}) = \Omega(Ld)$ with high probability over the noise. The second inequality absorbs the polynomial prefactor $P = \mathrm{poly}(\mathsf{N}, L, d, 1/\xi, 1/\lambda, 1/\omega)$ into the exponent: for $\alpha\varepsilon^2{\sf T}/(2\mathsf{N}) \ge 2\log P$ this is the standard absorption $P e^{-x} \le e^{-x/2}$; for smaller $\sf T$ --- a burn-in window of the same order as the Stage-I/II boundary, up to the $O(1)$ factor $\log P/\log({\sf N}Ld/\xi^2)$ --- the displayed exponential is read together with the crude branch, i.e.\ the upper-bound prefactor of Theorem~ef{thm:scaling_law} absorbs $P$ inside the burn-in window, where the bound asserts no more than $\Delta{\cal R}(F) = O({\cal L}(0,\mathbb{D}))$. We rename $\alpha/4$ as $\alpha$ below. Combining with Theorem~ef{thm:generalization} and Equation~\eqref{eq:approx_vareps} (using the statistical term $Ld\cdot\xi^2/{\sf N}$):  egin{align*} \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} \sup_{\mathbb{D} \in {\cal D}} \sqrt{\Delta{\cal R}(F)} \leq & ~ \exp\Big(- rac{\alpha \varepsilon^2 \mathsf{T}}{\mathsf{N}}\Big) \cdot \sqrt{{\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D})} + \sqrt{4\varepsilon^2 + Ld \cdot O\Big( rac{\xi^2}{\sf N} + \xi\varepsilon\Big)} \ \leq & ~ \exp\Big(- rac{\alpha \varepsilon^2 \mathsf{T}}{\mathsf{N}}\Big) \cdot \sqrt{{\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D})} + 2\varepsilon + O\Big( rac{\xi}{{\sf N}^{1/2}} + (\xi\varepsilon)^{1/2}\Big) \ \leq & ~ \exp\Big(- rac{\alpha \varepsilon^2 \mathsf{T}}{\mathsf{N}}\Big) \cdot \sqrt{{\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D})} + O\Big( rac{\xi}{{\sf N}^{1/2}} + (\xi\varepsilon)^{1/2}\Big), \end{align*} where the second step uses $\sqrt{a+b} \leq \sqrt{a}+\sqrt{b}$ for $a,b\geq 0$, and the third step absorbs the $2\varepsilon$ summand into the $O(\cdot)$ since $\varepsilon = \xi/{\sf N} \leq \xi/{\sf N}^{1/2}$ in this regime. We square both sides of the previous bound to obtain a bound on $\Delta{\cal R}(F)$ itself:  egin{align} \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} \sup_{\mathbb{D} \in {\cal D}} \Delta{\cal R}(F) \leq & ~ 2\exp\!\left(-2\alpha \varepsilon^2 \mathsf{T}/\mathsf{N}ight) \cdot {\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D}) + O\Big( rac{\xi^2}{{\sf N}} + \xi\varepsilon\Big), \end{align} using $(a+b)^2 \le 2a^2 + 2b^2$ and absorbing the constant $2$ into the $O(\cdot)$ on the second summand; the $1/\mathsf{N}$ in the exponent is the average-loss factor of Remark~ef{rem:n_in_rate}. For any total computational resource ${\sf C}$ with dataset size ${\sf N}$, we follow Definition~ef{def:gd} to require ${\sf M} = \Theta({\sf N}^3)$, and we choose $\varepsilon = \xi/{\sf N}$. Substituting:  egin{align*} \xi\varepsilon = \xi^2/{\sf N} \quad 	ext{and} \quad \alpha \varepsilon^2/\mathsf{N} = \alpha \xi^2/{\sf N}^3. \end{align*} {\it Condition 1 (Compute-Starved Stage).} When the optimization term $\exp(-2\alpha\varepsilon^2 \mathsf{T}/\mathsf{N})$ dominates the statistical $\xi^2/\mathsf{N}$ term, equivalently when:  egin{align*} & ~ {\sf T} \le  rac{\mathsf{N}\log({\sf N}\cdot Ld /\xi^2)}{2\alpha\varepsilon^2} =  rac{{\sf N}^3 \log({\sf N}\cdot Ld /\xi^2)}{2\alpha \xi^2}, \end{align*} which using ${\sf C} = O({\sf MTN})$ and ${\sf M} = {\sf N}^3$ translates into:  egin{align*} {\sf C} \leq  rac{{\sf N}^7\log( {\sf N} \cdot Ld/\xi^2)}{\xi^2}\quad 	ext{up to constants}, \end{align*} we have:  egin{align*} \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} \sup_{\mathbb{D} \in {\cal D}} \Delta{\cal R}(F) \leq & ~ C \exp\!\left(-\alpha \xi^2{\sf T}/{\sf N}^3ight) \cdot {\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D}) \ = & ~ C \exp\Big(-\alpha \xi^2  rac{{\sf MTN}}{{\sf N}^4{\sf M}}\Big) \cdot {\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D}) \ \leq & ~ C \exp\Big(-\alpha \xi^2  rac{{\sf C}}{{\sf N}^4{\sf M}}\Big) \cdot {\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D}) \ \leq & ~ C \exp\Big(-\alpha \xi^2  rac{{\sf C}}{{\sf N}^7}\Big) \cdot {\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D}), \end{align*} where the second equality multiplies and divides by ${\sf MN}$, the third inequality uses ${\sf C} = O({\sf MTN}) \geq {\sf NTM}/c$ for some constant $c$, and the fourth uses ${\sf M} \le {\sf N}^3$ in the exponent. The constant $C = \mathrm{poly}(L, d, 1/\lambda, 1/\omega)$. {\it Condition 2 (Data-Limited Stage).} When ${\sf T} > {\sf N}^3 \log({\sf N}\cdot Ld /\xi^2)/(2\alpha\xi^2)$, or equivalently:  egin{align*} {\sf C} = O({\sf MTN}) >  rac{{\sf M}{\sf N}^4\log( {\sf N} \cdot Ld/\xi^2)}{\xi^2} \iff {\sf C} >  rac{{\sf N}^7\log( {\sf N} \cdot Ld/\xi^2)}{\xi^2}, \end{align*} the optimization term decays faster than the statistical floor; the bound \eqref{eq:dr_bound} reduces to:  egin{align*} \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} \sup_{\mathbb{D} \in {\cal D}} \Delta{\cal R}(F) \leq & ~ O\Big( rac{\xi^2}{{\sf N}} \Big). \end{align*} We now optimize over ${\sf N}$ subject to the compute budget. The constraint is $\xi^{-2}\,{\sf N}^7\log({\sf N}\cdot Ld/\xi^2) \le {\sf C}$. Writing $u := {\sf N}^7/\xi^2$, this becomes:  egin{align*} u\log(u^{1/7} \cdot \xi^{2/7} Ld) \leq {\sf C}, \end{align*} whose maximal solution satisfies (treating the slowly varying log factor via the Lambert $W$ function $W(\cdot)$, which inverts $z\mapsto z\log z$):  egin{align*} u_{\max} = O\Big(  rac{{\sf C}}{W({\sf C}/\xi^{12})}\Big), \quad	ext{so}\quad {\sf N}_{\max} = O\Big(  rac{{\sf C}\xi^2}{W({\sf C}/\xi^{12})} \Big)^{1/7}. \end{align*} Substituting back:  egin{align*} \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} \sup_{\mathbb{D} \in {\cal D}} \Delta{\cal R}(F) \leq & ~ O\Big( rac{\xi^2}{{\sf N}_{\max}} \Big) = \xi^{12/7} \cdot O\left(  rac{{\sf C}}{W({\sf C}/\xi^{12})} ight)^{-1/7} \leq \xi^{12/7} \cdot \widetilde{O}\left( {\sf C} ight)^{-1/7}, \end{align*} where $W(\cdot)$ is the Lambert $W$ function and $\widetilde O$ hides $\log {\sf C}$ factors. The exponent $-1/7$ is a direct consequence of the $1/\mathsf{N}$ factor in Theorem~ef{thm:convergence}.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality splits optimization and ERM error; integrate the residual drift for the optimization term, add the ERM bound, then compare the two terms to get the threshold and optimize ${\sf N}$ under the compute budget. The Stage II rate comes from inverting $u\log u\le{\sf C}$ with the Lambert $W$ function.

nodes.name: Triangle inequality
nodes.statement_short: Split the error at the ERM $F'$

nodes.name: Residual drift
nodes.statement:
We control the {\it optimization} term $\|F-F'\|_{L^F({\cal X})}$ via the kernel-stable gradient flow, carrying the $1/\mathsf{N}$ factor of Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence} (Remark~\ref{rem:n_in_rate}) through the integration. Bounding the residual weight movement after time $\sf T$:
    \begin{align*}
        & ~ \max_{\nu\in [N]} \max_{r \in [m]} \| w_{(\nu), r}({\sf T}) -  w_{(\nu), r}(+\infty) \|_2 \notag \\
        \leq & ~   \int_{\sf T}^\infty \max_{\nu\in [N]}\max_{r \in [m]}\Big\| \frac{\mathrm{d} {\cal L}(s, \mathbb{D})}{\mathrm{d} w_{(\nu), r}(s)} \Big\|_2 \mathrm{d} s \notag\\
        \leq & ~  \int_{\sf T}^\infty \varepsilon \cdot \sqrt{{\cal L}(s, \mathbb{D})  }\mathrm{d} s \notag\\
        \leq & ~ \varepsilon \int_{\sf T}^\infty \exp\Big(-\frac{\alpha \varepsilon^2 s}{2\mathsf{N}}\Big) \cdot \sqrt{ {\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D})}\mathrm{d} s \\
        = & ~ \frac{2\mathsf{N}}{\alpha \varepsilon} \exp\Big(-\frac{\alpha \varepsilon^2 \mathsf{T}}{2\mathsf{N}}\Big) \cdot \sqrt{{\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D})},
    \end{align*}
    where the first step follows from the gradient-flow update Equation~\eqref{eq:ODE_update} and Cauchy--Schwarz, the second step from Part~15 of Lemma~\ref{lem:helpful_bounds}, the third step from Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence} after taking square roots, and the last step is direct integration.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the gradient after time ${\sf T}$

nodes.name: Optimization term
nodes.statement_short: Turn parameter drift into function distance and absorb the prefactor

nodes.name: Add ERM bound
nodes.statement:
Combining with Theorem~\ref{thm:generalization} and Equation~\eqref{eq:approx_vareps} (using the statistical term $Ld\cdot\xi^2/{\sf N}$):
    \begin{align*}
        \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} \sup_{\mathbb{D} \in {\cal D}}  \sqrt{\Delta{\cal R}(F)} \leq & ~  \exp\Big(-\frac{\alpha \varepsilon^2 \mathsf{T}}{\mathsf{N}}\Big) \cdot \sqrt{{\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D})} + \sqrt{4\varepsilon^2 + Ld \cdot O\Big(\frac{\xi^2}{\sf N} + \xi\varepsilon\Big)} \\
        \leq & ~ \exp\Big(-\frac{\alpha \varepsilon^2 \mathsf{T}}{\mathsf{N}}\Big) \cdot \sqrt{{\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D})} + 2\varepsilon + O\Big(\frac{\xi}{{\sf N}^{1/2}} + (\xi\varepsilon)^{1/2}\Big) \\
        \leq & ~ \exp\Big(-\frac{\alpha \varepsilon^2 \mathsf{T}}{\mathsf{N}}\Big) \cdot \sqrt{{\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D})} + O\Big(\frac{\xi}{{\sf N}^{1/2}} + (\xi\varepsilon)^{1/2}\Big),
    \end{align*}
    where the second step uses $\sqrt{a+b} \leq \sqrt{a}+\sqrt{b}$ for $a,b\geq 0$, and the third step absorbs the $2\varepsilon$ summand into the $O(\cdot)$ since $\varepsilon = \xi/{\sf N} \leq \xi/{\sf N}^{1/2}$ in this regime.
nodes.statement_short: Add the generalization bound of the ERM

nodes.name: Square
nodes.statement_short: Square to bound the excess risk; substitute $\varepsilon=\xi/{\sf N}$, ${\sf M}={\sf N}^3$

nodes.name: Condition 1
nodes.statement_short: Compute-starved stage: the exponential term dominates

nodes.name: Condition 2
nodes.statement_short: Data-limited stage: statistical floor, then optimize ${\sf N}$ under the budget

nodes.name: Statistical floor
nodes.statement_short: Above the threshold the bound reduces to $O(\xi^2/{\sf N})$

nodes.name: Optimize N
nodes.statement_short: Invert the budget constraint with the Lambert $W$ function

nodes.name: Squared excess-risk bound
nodes.statement: \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} \sup_{\mathbb{D} \in {\cal D}} \Delta{\cal R}(F) \leq & ~ 2\exp\!\left(-2\alpha \varepsilon^2 \mathsf{T}/\mathsf{N}\right) \cdot {\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D}) + O\Big(\frac{\xi^2}{{\sf N}} + \xi\varepsilon\Big),
nodes.label: eq:dr_bound

nodes.name: Single-variable scaling laws
nodes.statement: Let all pre-conditions hold as Corollary~\ref{cor:approximation}. Then, with a probability at least $1 - \delta$, there exists: \begin{itemize} \item {\bf Time-Law.} We fix the dataset set ${\sf N}$ and model size ${\sf M} = \Omega({\sf N}^3)$, and choosing $\varepsilon = \xi/{\sf N}$, we have $\inf_{{\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} \sup_{\mathbb{D} \in {\cal D}} \Delta{\cal R}(F) \leq \exp(-\alpha\,\xi^2\,{\sf T}/{\sf N}^3) + O(\frac{\xi^2}{{\sf N}} )$. \item {\bf Data-Law.} For any dataset size ${\sf N}$, we let $\varepsilon = \xi/{\sf N}$, ${\sf M} = \Omega({\sf N}^3)$ and $T = \widetilde{\Omega}(\frac{{\sf N}^3\log({\sf N}\cdot Ld/\xi^2)}{\xi^2})$, we have: $\inf_{{\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} \sup_{\mathbb{D} \in {\cal D}} \Delta{\cal R}(F) \leq O(\frac{\xi^2}{{\sf N}} )$. \item {\bf Model-Law.} We fix the dataset set ${\sf N}$ and let training time $T = \widetilde{\Omega}(\frac{{\sf M}^{2\zeta}\mathsf{N}\log({\sf N}\cdot Ld/\xi^2)}{\xi^2})$, where $\zeta \in (0, 1/3]$. Choosing $\varepsilon = \xi/{\sf M}^{\zeta}$, in the regime ${\sf N}^3 \le {\sf M} \le {\sf N}^{1/\zeta}$, we have $\inf_{{\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} \sup_{\mathbb{D} \in {\cal D}} $ $ \Delta{\cal R}(F) \leq \xi^2 {\sf M}^{-\zeta}$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Time law $\exp(-\alpha\xi^2{\sf T}/{\sf N}^3)+O(\xi^2/{\sf N})$, data law $O(\xi^2/{\sf N})$, and model law $\xi^2{\sf M}^{-\zeta}$ for ${\sf N}^3\le{\sf M}\le{\sf N}^{1/\zeta}$.
assumptions: Let all pre-conditions hold as Corollary~\ref{cor:approximation}
nodes.label: thm:single_law

nodes.name: Statistical lower bound (Le Cam two-point)
nodes.statement: Let $K$ be the layer-aggregated NTK at initialization, $K(x,y):=\sum_{\nu\in[N]}H_{(\nu),x,y}(0)$, and $\mathcal{H}_K$ its associated RKHS. Suppose there exists a non-zero element $g\in {\cal H}_K$ with $\|g\|_{L^F({\cal X})}>0$. Assume the noise $\Xi$ has each token-coordinate $\Xi_{\ell, k}$ Gaussian with variance $\xi^2$ (the standard sub-Gaussian assumption strengthens this to a constant factor; see Remark~\ref{rem:non_gaussian}). Let $\widehat F := \widehat F(\mathbb{D})$ denote any (deterministic or randomized) measurable estimator of $F^*$ from a dataset $\mathbb{D}$ of size $\sf N$. Then there exist absolute constants $c_1, c_2>0$ such that: \begin{align*} \inf_{\widehat F} \sup_{F^*\in {\cal H}_K} {\mathbb{E}}_{\mathbb{D}\sim {\cal D}^{\otimes {\sf N}}}\big[\Delta{\cal R}(\widehat F)\big] \ge c_1 \cdot \frac{\xi^2}{{\sf N}}. \end{align*}
nodes.section: J.4 Statistical Lower Bound (Le Cam Two-Point Method)
nodes.statement_short: Every estimator suffers excess risk at least $\xi^2/(16{\sf N})$ for some target in the NTK RKHS.
assumptions: Suppose there exists a non-zero element $g\in {\cal H}_K$ with $\|g\|_{L^F({\cal X})}>0$
Assume the noise $\Xi$ has each token-coordinate $\Xi_{\ell, k}$ Gaussian with variance $\xi^2$
nodes.label: thm:lower_stat

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem J.9
nodes.statement: \textbf{Step 1: Two-point construction.} Let $g\in {\cal H}_K$ be the non-zero element fixed by hypothesis, normalized so that $\|g\|_{L^F({\cal X})}=1$. Define the two-point family: \begin{align*} F_0^* := 0, \qquad F_1^* := \rho \cdot g, \qquad \rho := \sqrt{\frac{\xi^2}{2{\sf N}}}. \end{align*} Both lie in ${\cal H}_K$. \textbf{Step 2: Bound the KL divergence.} Under each $F_j^*$, the data law is $\mathcal{D}_j = {\cal X}\times \mathcal{N}(F_j^*(X), \xi^2 I_{Ld})$, so the per-sample KL divergence is \begin{align*} D_{\rm KL}({\cal D}_0\|{\cal D}_1) = {\mathbb{E}}_X\Big[\frac{1}{2\xi^2}\|F_0^*(X) - F_1^*(X)\|_F^2\Big] = \frac{\rho^2}{2\xi^2} \cdot \|g\|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2 = \frac{\rho^2}{2\xi^2}. \end{align*} For an i.i.d.\ dataset of size $\sf N$, $D_{\rm KL}({\cal D}_0^{\otimes {\sf N}}\|{\cal D}_1^{\otimes {\sf N}}) = {\sf N}\cdot \rho^2/(2\xi^2)$. With our choice $\rho^2 = \xi^2/(2{\sf N})$, we have: \begin{align*} D_{\rm KL}({\cal D}_0^{\otimes {\sf N}}\|{\cal D}_1^{\otimes {\sf N}}) = \frac{1}{4} \le \log 2. \end{align*} \textbf{Step 3: Apply Le Cam's two-point lemma} (Theorem 2.2 of \citealp{tsy09}). For any estimator $\widehat F$: \begin{align*} \inf_{\widehat F}\sup_{j\in\{0,1\}} {\mathbb{E}}_{\mathbb{D}\sim {\cal D}_j^{\otimes{\sf N}}}\big[\|\widehat F-F_j^*\|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2\big] \ge \frac{1}{4}\big(1-\sqrt{D_{\rm KL}/2}\big)\cdot \|F_0^*-F_1^*\|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2. \end{align*} Substituting the bound on KL: \begin{align*} \inf_{\widehat F}\sup_{j\in\{0,1\}} {\mathbb{E}}\big[\|\widehat F-F_j^*\|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2\big] \ge \frac{1}{4}\big(1 - \sqrt{1/8}\big)\cdot \rho^2 \ge \frac{1}{8}\cdot \frac{\xi^2}{2{\sf N}} = \frac{\xi^2}{16{\sf N}}. \end{align*} \textbf{Step 4: Translate to excess risk.} By Equation~\eqref{eq:bound_delta_R}, $\Delta{\cal R}(F) = \|F - F^*\|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2$, so: \begin{align*} \inf_{\widehat F}\sup_{F^*\in{\cal H}_K} {\mathbb{E}}\big[\Delta{\cal R}(\widehat F)\big] \ge \inf_{\widehat F}\sup_{j\in\{0,1\}} {\mathbb{E}}\big[\Delta{\cal R}(\widehat F)\big] \ge \frac{\xi^2}{16{\sf N}}, \end{align*} yielding the claim with $c_1 = 1/16$.
nodes.section: J.4 Statistical Lower Bound (Le Cam Two-Point Method)
nodes.statement_short: Le Cam two-point method with $F_0^*=0$ and $F_1^*=\rho g$, $\rho^2=\xi^2/(2{\sf N})$.

nodes.name: Step 1
nodes.statement_short: Two-point construction
nodes.section: J.4 Statistical Lower Bound (Le Cam Two-Point Method)

nodes.name: Step 2
nodes.statement_short: KL divergence of the two data laws is $1/4$
nodes.section: J.4 Statistical Lower Bound (Le Cam Two-Point Method)

nodes.name: Step 3
nodes.statement_short: Apply Le Cam's two-point lemma
nodes.section: J.4 Statistical Lower Bound (Le Cam Two-Point Method)

nodes.name: Step 4
nodes.statement_short: Translate to excess risk
nodes.section: J.4 Statistical Lower Bound (Le Cam Two-Point Method)

nodes.name: Non-Gaussian noise
nodes.statement: The assumption that $\Xi$ is Gaussian is used only to compute the KL divergence in closed form. For general centred sub-Gaussian noise with variance proxy $\xi^2$, the proof goes through with KL replaced by the Bhattacharyya / chi-squared divergence and yields the same $\Omega(\xi^2/{\sf N})$ rate up to an absolute constant; we adopt the Gaussian setting only for cleanest exposition.
nodes.section: J.4 Statistical Lower Bound (Le Cam Two-Point Method)
nodes.statement_short: For sub-Gaussian noise the same rate follows with another divergence, up to constants.
nodes.label: rem:non_gaussian

nodes.name: Lower bound on the data-limited stage
nodes.statement: Suppose ${\sf C} > {\sf N}^7\log({\sf N}\cdot Ld/\xi^2)/\xi^2$ (the data-limited regime of Theorem~\ref{thm:scaling_law:informal}). Then with the maximum admissible ${\sf N}_{\max} = O((\xi^2{\sf C}/W({\sf C}/\xi^{12}))^{1/7})$, we have: \begin{align*} \inf_{F\in{\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})}\sup_{\mathbb{D}\in{\cal D}}{\mathbb{E}}\big[\Delta{\cal R}(F)\big] \ge c_1' \cdot \xi^{12/7}\cdot \widetilde\Omega({\sf C}^{-1/7}), \end{align*} matching the upper bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:scaling_law} up to constants and logarithmic factors.
nodes.section: J.4 Statistical Lower Bound (Le Cam Two-Point Method)
nodes.statement_short: In the data-limited regime every model in the class has excess risk $\xi^{12/7}\widetilde\Omega({\sf C}^{-1/7})$.
assumptions: Suppose ${\sf C} > {\sf N}^7\log({\sf N}\cdot Ld/\xi^2)/\xi^2$ (the data-limited regime of Theorem~\ref{thm:scaling_law:informal})
nodes.label: cor:lower_data_limited

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary J.11
nodes.statement: The infimum over $F\in{\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})$ does not exceed the infimum over all measurable estimators of $F^*$ from $\mathbb{D}$, so Theorem~\ref{thm:lower_stat} applies and gives $\Omega(\xi^2/{\sf N})$ for any ${\sf N}$. Plugging in ${\sf N}=O((\xi^2{\sf C}/W({\sf C}/\xi^{12}))^{1/7})$: \begin{align*} \frac{\xi^2}{{\sf N}} = \xi^2 \cdot O\Big(\frac{W({\sf C}/\xi^{12})}{\xi^2{\sf C}}\Big)^{1/7} = \xi^{12/7}\cdot O\Big(\frac{{\sf C}}{W({\sf C}/\xi^{12})}\Big)^{-1/7}, \end{align*} which is the claim.
nodes.section: J.4 Statistical Lower Bound (Le Cam Two-Point Method)
nodes.statement_short: Apply the statistical lower bound and substitute the largest admissible ${\sf N}$.

nodes.name: First-order optimization method
nodes.statement: We consider any first-order optimization method ${\cal A}$ that produces a sequence $\theta(0), \theta(t_1), \theta(t_2), \dots$ inside the lazy-training ball of Definition~\ref{def:gd}, where each iterate depends only on previous gradient queries $\{\nabla_\theta {\cal L}(t_k, \mathbb{B}(t_k))\}_k$.
nodes.section: J.5 Optimization-Side Lower Bound (First-Order Oracle Complexity)

nodes.name: Optimization-side lower bound (first-order oracle complexity)
nodes.statement: Under Assumption~\ref{ass:positive_definite} and Definition~\ref{def:gd}, denote $\lambda_{\max}:= \max_{\nu\in[N]} \lambda_{\max}(H_{(\nu)}'(0)/\omega)$. There exist absolute constants $c_2, C_{\rm opt}>0$ such that for any first-order method ${\cal A}$ and any time horizon ${\sf T}\ge 0$, there exists a data distribution ${\cal D}$ and an initialization $\theta(0)$ for which: \begin{align*} {\cal L}({\sf T}, \mathbb{D}) \ge c_2\cdot \exp(-C_{\rm opt}\cdot \omega\lambda_{\max}\cdot \varepsilon^2 \cdot {\sf T}) \cdot {\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D}). \end{align*} Combined with the compute identity ${\sf C} = O({\sf MTN})$, ${\sf M}=\Theta({\sf N}^3)$, $\varepsilon = \xi/{\sf N}$, and the $1/\mathsf{N}$ factor in the rate (Remark~\ref{rem:n_in_rate}), this yields a lower bound on the excess risk in the {\it Compute-Starved Stage}: \begin{align*} \inf_{F\in{\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})}\sup_{\mathbb{D}\in{\cal D}} \Delta{\cal R}(F) \ge c_2'\cdot \exp(-C_{\rm opt}'\cdot \sqrt{\kappa}\,\xi^2{\sf C}/{\sf N}^7) \cdot {\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D}), \end{align*} matching the upper bound of Theorem~\ref{thm:scaling_law} up to a $\sqrt{\kappa}$ factor in the exponent (where $\kappa:=\lambda_{\max}/\lambda$); the $\sqrt{\kappa}$ gap reflects the difference between the spectral lower bound used in the upper-bound argument and the geometric-mean rate produced by the Nemirovski--Yudin lower bound, and is unavoidable for first-order methods.
nodes.section: J.5 Optimization-Side Lower Bound (First-Order Oracle Complexity)
nodes.statement_short: Some instance forces any first-order method to loss $\ge c\exp(-C\omega\lambda_{\max}\varepsilon^2{\sf T})$, giving a compute-starved lower bound matching up to $\sqrt\kappa$.
assumptions: Under Assumption~\ref{ass:positive_definite} and Definition~\ref{def:gd}
nodes.label: thm:lower_opt

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem J.12
nodes.statement:
extbf{Step 1: Reduction to a quadratic problem.} By Lemma~ef{lem:perturbations} and Definition~ef{def:gd}, the loss in the lazy regime is well approximated by its second-order expansion around $	heta(0)$:  egin{align*} {\cal L}(t,\mathbb{D}) =  rac{1}{2}\Delta	heta(t)^	op {\sf H} \Delta	heta(t) + \langle b, \Delta	heta(t)angle + {\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D}) + o(1), \end{align*} where $\Delta	heta(t) := 	heta(t)-	heta(0)$, ${\sf H}$ is the parameter-space Hessian assembled from $\{H_{(
u)}(0)\otimes I_d\}_{
u\in[N]}$, and $b$ is the residual gradient. The $o(1)$ correction is uniform on the lazy-training ball by Part~9--10 of Lemma~ef{lem:helpful_bounds}. Thus the optimization problem reduces (up to higher-order terms) to minimizing a quadratic with eigenvalue spread $[\omega\lambda/2,\;\omega\lambda_{\max}]$. 	extbf{Step 2: Apply Nemirovski--Yudin.} For any first-order method on a strongly convex quadratic with condition number $\kappa = \lambda_{\max}/\lambda_{\min}$, there exist initial conditions for which the loss after $T$ gradient queries satisfies (Theorem~2.1.13 of \citealp{nes03}; see also \citealp{ny83}):  egin{align*} {\cal L}(T) - {\cal L}^* \ge \Big( rac{\sqrt{\kappa}-1}{\sqrt{\kappa}+1}\Big)^{2T} \cdot ({\cal L}(0)-{\cal L}^*). \end{align*} Translating to the gradient-flow setting requires a continuous-time limit. The standard reduction takes step size $\eta = 1/\lambda_{\max}$ and substitutes $T 	o t/\eta = t\lambda_{\max}$:  egin{align*} \log\Big( rac{\sqrt\kappa - 1}{\sqrt\kappa + 1}\Big)^{2T} = -2T \log rac{\sqrt\kappa+1}{\sqrt\kappa - 1} \approx - rac{4T}{\sqrt\kappa} \end{align*} for $\kappa	o\infty$. Substituting $T	o t\lambda_{\max}$ gives an exponential decay of rate $4\lambda_{\max}/\sqrt\kappa = 4\sqrt{\lambda_{\min}\lambda_{\max}}$. As $\eta	o 0$ (continuous limit), the bound is preserved (it is step-size monotone in this regime), giving:  egin{align*} {\cal L}(t) - {\cal L}^* \ge \exp\Big(-4\sqrt{\lambda_{\min}\lambda_{\max}}\cdot t\Big)\cdot ({\cal L}(0)-{\cal L}^*). \end{align*} Since $\lambda_{\min}\ge \omega\lambda/2$ (Lemma~ef{lem:perturbations}) and $\lambda_{\max}\le \omega\lambda_{\max}^{(K)}$ where $\lambda_{\max}^{(K)} := \max_
u \lambda_{\max}(H_{(
u)}'(0)/\omega)$:  egin{align*} {\cal L}(t) \ge \exp ig(-C_{m opt}\cdot \omega\sqrt{\lambda \lambda_{\max}^{(K)}}\cdot t ig)\cdot {\cal L}(0). \end{align*} The geometric mean $\sqrt{\lambda\lambda_{\max}^{(K)}}$ is {\it not} a single constant: it differs from $\lambda$ by a factor of $\sqrt{\kappa}=\sqrt{\lambda_{\max}^{(K)}/\lambda}$, which is $\mathrm{poly}(L,d,1/\delta)^{1/2}$ rather than $O(1)$. We therefore retain $\sqrt{\kappa}$ explicitly in the exponent (this is the unavoidable Nemirovski--Yudin condition-number gap; see Appendix~ef{app_sub:matching_precise}). Including the $\varepsilon^2$ factor that arises when reading the loss in $L^F({\cal X})$ rather than parameter space (Part~15 of Lemma~ef{lem:helpful_bounds}, with the $1/n$ factor) and the $1/n$ from the average-loss normalization:  egin{align*} {\cal L}({\sf T}, \mathbb{D}) \ge c_2\cdot \exp\!\left(- rac{C_{m opt}\cdot \sqrt{\kappa}\,\omega\lambda N\cdot \varepsilon^2 \cdot {\sf T}}{n}ight)\cdot {\cal L}(0, \mathbb{D}). \end{align*} 	extbf{Step 3: Translate to compute.} Using ${\sf C} = O({\sf MTN})$, ${\sf M}=\Theta({\sf N}^3)$ (Definition~ef{def:gd}) and $\varepsilon = \xi/{\sf N}$ (the choice that defines the data-limited boundary in Theorem~ef{thm:scaling_law}), and absorbing $\omega N\lambda$ into the constant $\mathrm{poly}(L,d,B,\lambda)$:  egin{align*}  rac{\sqrt{\kappa}\,\omega\lambda N\varepsilon^2 {\sf T}}{n} = \sqrt{\kappa}\,\omega\lambda N\cdot  rac{\xi^2}{{\sf N}^2}\cdot  rac{{\sf C}}{{\sf MN}\cdot \mathsf{N}} =  rac{\sqrt{\kappa}\,\omega\lambda N\xi^2 {\sf C}}{{\sf N}^4 \cdot {\sf M}\cdot \mathsf{N}} \le \Theta\Big( rac{\sqrt{\kappa}\,\xi^2 {\sf C}}{{\sf N}^7}\Big), \end{align*} which yields:  egin{align*} \inf_{F\in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})}\sup_{\mathbb{D}\in{\cal D}}\Delta{\cal R}(F) \ge c_2'\cdot \exp\!\left(-C_{m opt}'\,\sqrt{\kappa}\,\xi^2{\sf C}/{\sf N}^7ight)\cdot {\cal L}(0,\mathbb{D}). \end{align*} The conversion from training-loss lower bound to excess-risk lower bound uses the standard fact that $\Delta {\cal R}(F)\ge \|F-F^*\|_{L^F({\cal X})}^2 - O(\xi^2/{\sf N})$ (cf.~Equation~\eqref{eq:bound_delta_R}), and the second term is dominated by the exponential in the Compute-Starved Stage where Equation~\eqref{eq:cond_C} fails.

nodes.statement_short: Reduce the lazy-regime loss to a quadratic, apply Nemirovski-Yudin lower bounds in the continuous limit, then translate to compute.

nodes.name: Tightness
nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{thm:lower_opt} together with Theorem~\ref{thm:scaling_law} yields a two-sided compute-starved bound: \begin{align*} \exp\big(-C_{\rm opt}'\,\sqrt{\kappa}\,\xi^2{\sf C}/{\sf N}^7\big)\cdot {\cal L}(0,\mathbb{D}) \;\le\; \inf_{F}\sup_\mathbb{D}\Delta{\cal R}(F) \;\le\; C\exp\big(-\alpha\,\xi^2{\sf C}/{\sf N}^7\big)\cdot {\cal L}(0,\mathbb{D}), \end{align*} where $\kappa=\lambda_{\max}/\lambda\le\mathrm{poly}(L,d,1/\delta)$. The two exponents differ by a factor of $\sqrt{\kappa}$: the upper-bound exponent is $\Theta(\lambda)$ (smallest eigenvalue of the kernel after normalization), the lower bound is $\Theta(\sqrt{\lambda\lambda_{\max}})$ (geometric mean), as is standard for first-order methods on quadratics. Combined with Corollary~\ref{cor:lower_data_limited}, the resulting two-stage scaling law $\Theta(\xi^{12/7}{\sf C}^{-1/7})$ in the data-limited stage is matching up to constants, logarithmic factors, and the $\sqrt{\kappa}$ gap. We adopt the language ``matching up to $\mathrm{poly}(L,d,\kappa)$'' (rather than ``minimax-tight'') to keep this distinction visible.
nodes.section: J.5 Optimization-Side Lower Bound (First-Order Oracle Complexity)
nodes.statement_short: Upper and lower compute-starved exponents differ by $\sqrt\kappa$; the data-limited law matches up to constants and logs.
nodes.label: rem:tightness

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem J.8
nodes.statement: {\bf Proof of Time-Law.} Under fixed ${\sf N}$ and ${\sf M} = \Omega({\sf N}^3)$, set $\varepsilon = \xi/{\sf N}$. Substituting into Equation~\eqref{eq:dr_bound} (whose optimization term is $\exp(-2\alpha\varepsilon^2{\sf T}/\mathsf{N})\cdot{\cal L}(0,\mathbb{D})$, with the $1/\mathsf{N}$ factor from Remark~\ref{rem:n_in_rate}) gives the bound directly: \begin{align*} \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} \sup_{\mathbb{D} \in {\cal D}} \Delta{\cal R}(F) \leq O\!\left(\exp(-\alpha\,\xi^2\,{\sf T}/{\sf N}^3)\right) + O\Big(\frac{\xi^2}{\sf N}\Big), \end{align*} so this proof reduces to {\it Condition 1} of Theorem~\ref{thm:scaling_law} with ${\sf C} = {\sf MTN}$, ${\sf M}, {\sf N}$ fixed. {\bf Proof of Data-Law.} Under $\varepsilon = \xi/{\sf N}$, ${\sf M} = \Omega({\sf N}^3)$, and $T = \widetilde\Omega({\sf N}^3\log/\xi^2)$ (so the optimization term $\exp(-\alpha\xi^2{\sf T}/{\sf N}^3)$ is exponentially small in $\log({\sf N}\cdot Ld/\xi^2)$), the bound \eqref{eq:dr_bound} reduces to its statistical floor $O(\xi^2/{\sf N})$, recovering {\it Condition 2} of Theorem~\ref{thm:scaling_law}. {\bf Proof of Model-Law.} Given $\zeta \in (0, 1/3]$, choose $\varepsilon = \xi/{\sf M}^\zeta$. Following {\it Condition 2} of Theorem~\ref{thm:scaling_law}, choose \begin{align*} {\sf T} = \frac{{\sf M}^{2\zeta}\,\mathsf{N}\,\log({\sf N}\cdot Ld/\xi^2)}{\xi^2}, \end{align*} so $\alpha\varepsilon^2 {\sf T}/\mathsf{N} = \alpha\log({\sf N}\cdot Ld/\xi^2)$, hence $\exp(-\alpha\varepsilon^2 {\sf T}/\mathsf{N}) = ({\sf N}\cdot Ld/\xi^2)^{-\alpha}$. For this to be $\leq \xi^2 {\sf M}^{-\zeta}$, we need $\alpha\log({\sf N}\cdot Ld/\xi^2) \ge \zeta\log\mathsf{M} - 2\log\xi$, equivalently $\alpha \ge (\zeta\log\mathsf{M}-2\log\xi)/\log(\mathsf{N}\cdot Ld/\xi^2)$. This is feasible whenever $\mathsf{M}\le \mathsf{N}^{1/\zeta}$ (so $\zeta\log\mathsf{M}\le \log\mathsf{N}$), i.e.\ in the regime stated in the theorem; we therefore restrict the Model-Law to ${\sf M}\le{\sf N}^{1/\zeta}$. Then: \begin{align*} {\sf C} = O({\sf MTN}) = \frac{{\sf M}^{2\zeta+1}{\sf N}^2\log({\sf N}\cdot Ld/\xi^2)}{\xi^2} \leq \frac{{\sf M}^{2\zeta + 5/3}\log({\sf N}\cdot Ld/\xi^2)}{\xi^2}, \end{align*} where the inequality uses ${\sf N} \leq {\sf M}^{1/3}$ (since ${\sf M} \geq {\sf N}^3$). The Model-Law regime is the part of parameter space where the bound from $\xi\varepsilon$ dominates over $\xi^2/{\sf N}$, i.e.~$\xi^2/{\sf N} \leq \xi\varepsilon = \xi^2/{\sf M}^\zeta$, which holds when ${\sf M}^\zeta \leq {\sf N}$, i.e.~${\sf M} \leq {\sf N}^{1/\zeta}$. Combined with ${\sf M} \geq {\sf N}^3$ and the feasibility condition above, this gives the regime ${\sf N}^3 \leq {\sf M} \leq {\sf N}^{1/\zeta}$ stated in the theorem. In this regime: \begin{align*} \inf_{F \in {\cal F}_{\sf M, T, N}(\mathbb{D})} \sup_{\mathbb{D} \in {\cal D}} \Delta{\cal R}(F) \leq \xi^2 {\sf M}^{-\zeta}, \end{align*} as claimed.
